mk1-r4.title: Ghép tiêu đề: khoa học về giấc ngủ
mk1-r4.instr: Bài đọc dài khoảng 750 từ như đề thật. Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Có 8 tiêu đề cho 7 đoạn, một tiêu đề thừa.
mk1-r4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: A third of our lives | Screens in the bedroom | Simple habits that help | Sleep is a waste of time | The myth of catching up | The price of a short night | The teenage clock | What happens while we sleep
Most of us spend around a third of our lives asleep, yet for most of history sleep was treated as a simple period of rest, when the body and mind switched off. Only in the last fifty years have scientists begun to understand how active and complex this state really is. Modern research suggests that sleep is not a luxury that busy people can afford to cut, but one of the foundations of good health, as important as diet and exercise. Understanding why we sleep, and what happens when we do not get enough, has therefore become a major field of study. Doctors now ask about sleep as routinely as they ask about smoking or alcohol, and governments in several countries have launched campaigns to encourage people to rest more. = A third of our lives
During the night, the brain moves through several cycles, each lasting about ninety minutes. In the deepest stage, the body repairs muscles and strengthens the immune system. In another stage, known as REM sleep, the brain becomes highly active and most dreaming takes place. Researchers believe this stage plays a key role in organising memories, deciding what to keep and what to forget. Students who sleep well after studying, for example, tend to remember new information far better than those who stay up late revising. Interrupting these cycles, for instance by setting an alarm in the middle of deep sleep, explains why people sometimes wake up feeling worse than when they went to bed. = What happens while we sleep
Parents often complain that teenagers refuse to go to bed and then cannot get up in the morning. Scientists now say this is not simply laziness. During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts, so teenagers naturally feel sleepy later at night and wake later in the morning. Some schools have responded by starting lessons an hour later, and early studies report better attendance, improved concentration and even fewer road accidents among young drivers. Not everyone is convinced, however. Some parents worry that later start times make it harder for them to get to work, and some teachers argue that teenagers would simply go to bed even later. = The teenage clock
Regularly sleeping less than seven hours a night has been linked to a wide range of problems. In the short term, people find it harder to concentrate, make more mistakes and become irritable. Over months and years, lack of sleep increases the risk of weight gain, heart disease and depression. Economists have even calculated the cost to businesses: tired employees are less productive and take more sick days, which costs some countries billions of dollars every year. Some researchers argue that a tired driver can be as dangerous as one who has drunk alcohol, which makes sleep a matter of public safety as well as personal health. = The price of a short night
One of the biggest enemies of sleep today is the smartphone. The blue light from screens tells the brain that it is still daytime, delaying the release of the hormone that makes us feel sleepy. In addition, checking messages or social media keeps the mind alert at exactly the moment it should be slowing down. Many experts therefore recommend switching off devices at least an hour before bed, and keeping phones out of the bedroom altogether. Reading a paper book or listening to calm music are often suggested as better ways of preparing the mind for rest. = Screens in the bedroom
Many people believe they can make up for a week of short nights by sleeping late at the weekend. Unfortunately, the evidence suggests this works only partly. While an extra few hours can reduce tiredness, it does not fully reverse the effects on memory and concentration. Worse, sleeping much later on Saturday and Sunday can confuse the body's clock, making it even harder to fall asleep on Sunday night and creating a kind of weekly jet lag. A regular routine across all seven days, rather than occasional long lie-ins, is therefore considered far more effective. = The myth of catching up
The good news is that small changes can make a real difference. Going to bed and getting up at the same time every day, even at weekends, helps to keep the body clock stable. A cool, dark and quiet bedroom encourages deeper sleep, while avoiding coffee in the afternoon and heavy meals late in the evening also helps. Above all, experts say, we need to stop seeing sleep as wasted time and start treating it as an investment in our health. People who still feel exhausted despite following this advice should see a doctor, as ongoing tiredness can be a sign of a medical condition that needs treatment. = Simple habits that help

When I moved into my first flat, I couldn't cook at all.
At first, I lived on instant noodles and takeaway food.
After a few months, however, I started to feel tired and unhealthy.
So I decided to sign up for a weekend cooking course.
There, a chef taught us how to make simple, healthy meals.
Now I cook dinner for my flatmates at least three times a week.

mk2-r2b.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại thành đoạn văn hợp lý.
mk2-r2b.body:
Five years ago, the only library in our neighbourhood was closed because of budget cuts.
Local residents were upset, as many children had used it to do their homework.
A group of parents then decided to open a small library of their own.
They collected unwanted books from neighbours and set up shelves in an empty shop.
Today, this volunteer-run library is open six days a week.
It has even started offering free English classes for adults.

mk2-r3.intro:
Lan: Tourism has brought a lot of money into our town. My parents opened a small guesthouse ten years ago, and it now supports our whole family. Of course, the streets are crowded in summer, but I think that's a fair price for the jobs it has created.

Mark: I've lived here all my life, and honestly, I hardly recognise the place anymore. Traditional shops have been replaced by souvenir stalls, and rents have risen so much that young locals can't afford to stay. I'm not against visitors, but the town council should limit the number of new hotels.

Sofia: I work as a tour guide, so tourism is my living. What worries me is the damage to the old temples. Some visitors climb on the walls to take photos. I'd like to see stricter rules and perhaps a small entrance fee to pay for repairs.

David: I moved here because of the lively atmosphere that tourists bring – the cafés, the festivals, the mix of languages. The town would be rather dull without them. Still, I agree that public transport hasn't kept up with the number of people.

mk2-r4.title: Ghép tiêu đề: tâm lý mua sắm
mk2-r4.instr: Bài đọc dài khoảng 750 từ như đề thật. Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Có 8 tiêu đề cho 7 đoạn, một tiêu đề thừa.
mk2-r4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Designed to keep us inside | Fear of missing out | Learning to shop wisely | One click away | Online shops will soon replace all stores | Shopping is never purely practical | The power of the first price | When choice becomes a burden
We like to think that we buy things because we need them. In reality, many of our purchases are driven by emotions, habits and clever techniques used by sellers. Psychologists who study consumer behaviour have found that the decision to buy is often made in seconds, long before we have carefully compared prices or considered whether we really want the product. Understanding these hidden influences can help shoppers make better choices, and it also explains why shops are designed in the way they are. In fact, studies using brain scans show that the areas linked to pleasure become active as soon as we see something we like, sometimes before we have even checked the price. = Shopping is never purely practical
One of the most effective techniques is known as 'anchoring'. When customers see a high original price crossed out next to a lower sale price, the first number acts as an anchor, making the second seem like a bargain, even if it is not particularly cheap. Restaurants use a similar trick by placing one very expensive dish at the top of the menu, which makes the other options look reasonable by comparison. In both cases, the first figure we notice shapes how we judge everything that follows. Many shoppers are aware of the trick, yet experiments show that even experts are influenced by it. Some online sellers even raise their 'original' prices shortly before a sale so that the discount looks larger. = The power of the first price
The layout of a supermarket is rarely accidental. Basic items such as milk and bread are usually placed at the back, so that customers have to walk past hundreds of other products to reach them. Pleasant music, the smell of fresh bread and the absence of clocks all encourage people to stay longer, and research shows that the longer shoppers stay, the more they spend. Even the height of the shelves is planned, with the most profitable products placed at eye level. Children's sweets, meanwhile, are often placed on lower shelves near the checkout, exactly where young shoppers can see and reach them while their parents wait in the queue. = Designed to keep us inside
Sellers also take advantage of our fear of missing an opportunity. Messages such as 'only three left in stock' or 'offer ends at midnight' create a sense of urgency that pushes people to decide quickly. Because nobody likes the feeling of having lost a good deal, many customers buy immediately rather than taking time to think, even when the shortage is not real and the same offer appears again the following week. Countdown clocks on websites, which show how many minutes remain before a discount expires, work in exactly the same way. = Fear of missing out
Online shopping has made these effects even stronger. With saved card details and one-click payment, the gap between wanting something and owning it has almost disappeared. Websites track what we look at and show us personalised adverts for days afterwards. Some studies suggest that people spend significantly more when they pay by card or phone than with cash, because digital money simply does not feel as real as notes and coins in a wallet. Free delivery offers also encourage people to add extra items to their basket simply to reach the minimum amount required. = One click away
Surprisingly, having more choice does not always make us happier. In a famous experiment, shoppers who were offered twenty-four types of jam were far less likely to buy any than those offered only six. Faced with too many options, people worry about making the wrong decision and may leave without buying anything, or feel less satisfied with what they eventually choose because they keep wondering about the alternatives. For this reason, some successful companies deliberately reduce the number of products they sell, making the decision easier for their customers. = When choice becomes a burden
None of this means that shoppers are helpless. Simple strategies, such as writing a list before going to the supermarket, waiting twenty-four hours before making large online purchases, and setting a monthly budget, can greatly reduce unplanned spending. Being aware of the techniques used by sellers is perhaps the most important step of all, since a trick that we recognise quickly loses much of its power over us. Some people also find it useful to unsubscribe from marketing emails and to remove saved card details from shopping websites, so that every purchase requires a moment of thought. = Learning to shop wisely

mk1-core5-v3.body:
LỰA CHỌN: caught | do | give | held | left | make | raised | risen | say | took
She ___ her umbrella on the bus this morning. = left
Prices have ___ by 10% this year. = risen
He ___ a cold after walking in the rain. = caught
I'd like to ___ a complaint about the service. = make
Can you ___ me a favour? = do

mk1-core5-v4.title: Từ vựng: cụm từ đi kèm
mk1-core5-v4.instr: Chọn từ thường đi cùng với từ bên trái (collocation).
mk1-core5-v4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: a business | a cloud | a colour | a joke | a river | a song | a table | the moon | the train | weight
book = a table
miss = the train
tell = a joke
run = a business
lose = weight

mk1-core5-v5.title: Từ vựng: ghép định nghĩa (nâng cao)
mk1-core5-v5.instr: Chọn từ phù hợp với từng định nghĩa (từ vựng B2).
mk1-core5-v5.body:
LỰA CHỌN: claim | deny | destroy | examine | expand | ignore | improve | maintain | neglect | shrink
to make something better = improve
to say that something is true without proof = claim
to become bigger in size or amount = expand
to keep something in good condition = maintain
to look at something very carefully = examine

mk2-core4-g.title: Ngữ pháp: 25 câu
mk2-core4-g.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng để hoàn thành câu. Đề thật có 25 câu, mỗi câu 3 lựa chọn; một số câu là ngữ pháp văn nói (đối thoại A–B).
mk2-core4-g.body:
This is the first time I ___ sushi.
*have eaten
ate
eat
? "It's the first time…" → hiện tại hoàn thành.

If it ___ tomorrow, we'll cancel the picnic.
*rains
will rain
rained
? Điều kiện loại 1: If + hiện tại đơn.

The windows ___ every week.
*are cleaned
clean
are cleaning
? Bị động hiện tại đơn.

The reason ___ I called is to invite you to dinner.
*why
which
where
? the reason why.

She asked me where I ___.
*lived
do live
did I live
? Câu hỏi gián tiếp: không đảo ngữ, lùi thì.

Students ___ use their phones during the exam.
*are not allowed to
don't have to
needn't
? not allowed to = không được phép.

I'll never forget ___ the Eiffel Tower for the first time.
*seeing
to see
see
? forget + V-ing: nhớ mãi việc đã làm.

By the time you arrive, we ___ dinner.
*will have finished
will finish
finish
? "By the time…" (tương lai) → tương lai hoàn thành.

A: Do you want tea or coffee?  B: ___ is fine.
*Either
Neither
Both
? Either = cái nào cũng được.

He refused ___ me the money.
*to lend
lending
lend
? refuse + to V.

If I ___ rich, I'd travel around the world.
*were
am
will be
? Điều kiện loại 2 dùng "were" cho mọi ngôi.

My new phone is much ___ than my old one.
*lighter
more light
lightest
? So sánh hơn của tính từ ngắn: -er + than.

Hardly ___ arrived when it started to rain.
*had we
we had
did we
? Đảo ngữ: Hardly had + S + V3 … when.

They made us ___ for two hours.
*wait
to wait
waiting
? make + O + V nguyên mẫu.

There aren't ___ chairs for everyone.
*enough
enough of
much
? enough + danh từ.

You ___ have locked the door – I saw it open.
*can't
mustn't
needn't
? can't have + V3: chắc chắn không.

A: Could you help me with this box?  B: ___.
*Of course
Of course not
Yes, I could
? Đồng ý giúp: Of course.

We ___ each other since we were children.
*have known
know
are knowing
? "know" không dùng tiếp diễn; since → hiện tại hoàn thành.

She's very interested ___ photography.
*in
on
at
? interested in.

She went to bed early ___ she was tired.
*because
because of
despite
? because + mệnh đề.

He hasn't called me ___.
*yet
already
just
? yet dùng trong câu phủ định, đứng cuối câu.

The documents must ___ by Friday.
*be signed
sign
signed
? Động từ khuyết thiếu + be + V3 (bị động).

A: Excuse me, is this seat free?  B: ___.
*Yes, go ahead
Yes, it free
No, thank you
? Mời ai ngồi: Yes, go ahead.

She ___ be very shy, but now she's confident.
*used to
is used to
was used
? used to + V: trước đây từng.

It was ___ a nice day that we had a picnic.
*such
so
too
? such + a + adj + N + that.

mk2-core4-v1.title: Từ vựng: từ đồng nghĩa
mk2-core4-v1.instr: Chọn từ có nghĩa gần nhất với từ bên trái. 10 lựa chọn, 5 lựa chọn không dùng đến.
mk2-core4-v1.body:
LỰA CHỌN: break | close | difficult | easy | never | open | payment | perhaps | present | repair
hard = difficult
fix = repair
shut = close
maybe = perhaps
gift = present

mk2-core4-v2.title: Từ vựng: ghép định nghĩa
mk2-core4-v2.instr: Chọn từ phù hợp với từng định nghĩa.
mk2-core4-v2.body:
LỰA CHỌN: bakery | bathroom | conductor | director | kitchen | pilot | receipt | secretary | supermarket | ticket
a person who checks tickets on a train = conductor
a piece of paper that shows what you have paid = receipt
a person who manages a company = director
a room where food is cooked = kitchen
a large shop that sells food and household goods = supermarket

mk2-core4-v3.title: Từ vựng: hoàn thành câu
mk2-core4-v3.instr: Chọn từ phù hợp nhất cho mỗi chỗ trống.
mk2-core4-v3.body:
LỰA CHỌN: away | gave | look | looking | off | on | out | put | seeing | take
I'm really ___ forward to the holiday. = looking
Can you ___ after my cat this weekend? = look
She ___ up smoking last year. = gave
We've run ___ of milk, so I'll buy some. = out
Please turn ___ the TV – I'm trying to sleep. = off

mk2-core4-v4.title: Từ vựng: cụm từ đi kèm
mk2-core4-v4.instr: Chọn từ thường đi cùng với từ bên trái (collocation).
mk2-core4-v4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: card | dinner | flower | hour | jam | job | music | river | sky | transport
public = transport
part-time = job
rush = hour
credit = card
traffic = jam

mk2-core4-v5.title: Từ vựng: từ đồng nghĩa (nâng cao)
mk2-core4-v5.instr: Chọn từ có nghĩa gần nhất với từ bên trái (từ vựng B2).
mk2-core4-v5.body:
LỰA CHỌN: about | at first | because | exactly | finally | however | now | previously | similarly | therefore
approximately = about
consequently = therefore
nevertheless = however
initially = at first
currently = now

mk1-lt5-p1.title: Nghe và chọn chi tiết
mk1-lt5-p1.instr: Nghe từng đoạn và chọn đáp án đúng. Mỗi đoạn được nghe tối đa 2 lần.
mk1-lt5-p1.body:
Listen to an announcement. Which platform to wait for the train?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q1.mp3
W: Attention, all passengers! The 10:30 train to Greenfield is now arriving at Platform 2. Please make sure you have your ticket ready before boarding. This train will stop at River Station and Oakwood before reaching its final destination.
*Platform 2
Platform 5
Platform 8

An artist is talking about her job. What is the difference in her job?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q2.mp3
W: Hello, my name is Sarah, and I'm an artist. My job is very fun, but I work irregular hours, sometimes late at night or on weekends. When I have inspiration, I paint for many hours without a break.
She works from 9 to 5
She doesn't work on weekends
*She works irregular hours

Listen to a conversation between the teacher and a parent. What will the father do?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q3.mp3
W: Teacher: I know a private tutor who works well with children. She can provide extra help and support. Father: That sounds like a good idea! Can you give me her contact information?
Enroll him in summer school
*Arrange private classes for his son
Talk to the principal

A woman is talking about her weekends. What did she do last week?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q4.mp3
W: My weekends are not always the same. Last weekend, I stayed at home and enjoyed some quiet moments with a book. I also watched a few movies and cooked a nice dinner for myself.
Went hiking
*Stayed at home
Attended a party

A teacher and a student are talking about transportation. How does the teacher go to school?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q5.mp3
W: Student: I usually take the bus. Teacher: I understand. I walk to school every day. It helps me get some exercise, and I enjoy the fresh air. I often walk with a few other teachers.
He drives
He takes the bus
*He walks

Anne is calling her daughter Sally. What does Anne need?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q6.mp3
W: Hi Sally, it's Mom. Can you stop by the store on your way home? We're out of eggs, and I need some to finish baking the cake. Thanks, sweetie!
*Eggs
Bread
Milk

A mom is talking to her son. What does he like to study?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q7.mp3
W: Hey sweetheart. Your art project looks amazing, you're really talented. I love how you used all those bright colors. You always do such a great job with your drawings. But remember, you also need to spend some time on math and science.
*Art
Science
History

A woman is talking about her family's holidays. What did the family do last year?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q8.mp3
W: This year, my family and I are going to the beach for our holiday. Last year, we went camping on the mountain, which was fun, but this time we wanted to do something different.
Traveled abroad
*Camping
Went to the beach

A man is talking about how he goes to work. Why does he prefer traveling by train?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q9.mp3
W: After thinking about all the choices, I decided to travel by train. It's practical because it's on time, and I can relax during the trip. Plus, the station is close to my office!
It's cheaper than biking
*It's practical
It's faster than flying

Listen to the instructions of a university. Where is the main office?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q10.mp3
W: Welcome to our university! If you need help with anything, the main office is on the first floor of the center campus building. There, you can ask about classes, schedules, or anything else.
On the third floor
*On the first floor
In the basement

A woman is talking about shopping places. Where is she going to go shopping?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q11.mp3
W: I love shopping, and there are so many places to choose from in our city. This time, I'm excited to check out the new shopping center that just opened. I've heard it has everything I need in one place!
At the downtown market
*At a new shopping center
At the mall

A tour guide is making an announcement. Why was the tour canceled?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q12.mp3
W: The weather is perfect and transportation is not a problem, everything is ready for our trip. Unfortunately, we don't have enough people for the tour today. Because of this, we have to cancel the tour.
*Not enough people
Bad weather
Transportation problems

A man is talking about his job. What does the man want to do next?
AUDIO: audio/t5_q13.mp3
W: I used to be a chef. After that I became a history teacher. Teaching was rewarding, but I wanted to try something new. Now, I want to become a writer! I have many ideas for stories in my mind.
*Become a writer
Become a chef again
Start teaching history again

mk1-lt5-p2.title: Ghép người nói
mk1-lt5-p2.instr: Four people are talking about online shopping. Match each speaker with what they say.
mk1-lt5-p2.body:
LỰA CHỌN: It saves time. | It is cheaper. | Products are delivered. | There are more choices.
Speaker A = It saves time.
AUDIO: audio/t5_q14_1.mp3
W: I've always been a bit short on time, especially with my busy work schedule. That's why I prefer shopping online - it really helps me save so much time. Instead of spending hours in stores, I can quickly browse and make my purchase in just a few clicks.
Speaker B = It is cheaper.
AUDIO: audio/t5_q14_2.mp3
W: For me, one of the main reasons I shop online is because it's usually more affordable. I've noticed that many online stores offer discounts and I can often find cheaper prices than I would in physical shops.
Speaker C = Products are delivered.
AUDIO: audio/t5_q14_3.mp3
W: The biggest advantage of shopping online for me is the fact that I don't have to leave my house. I love how products get delivered straight to my doorstep, especially when I order something heavy or large.
Speaker D = There are more choices.
AUDIO: audio/t5_q14_4.mp3
W: What I love about shopping online is the incredible variety of products available. When I go to a store, I'm limited to what's in stock, but online, there's so much more choice. I can find different brands, styles, and even hard-to-find sizes.

mk1-lt5-p3.audio:
AUDIO: audio/t5_q15.mp3
M: I believe exhibitions should be different. They need to show new ideas, not just the same old things.
W: Sometimes, it's nice to celebrate our traditions, even if they are losing significance.
W: I worry that the local festivals will disappear soon.
W: Let's not forget how important schools are in keeping our traditions alive.
mk1-lt5-p3.title: Ai có ý kiến này?
mk1-lt5-p3.instr: A man and a woman are talking about the local center that was recently opened. Decide whose opinion matches each statement: the man, the woman, or both. You can listen twice.
mk1-lt5-p3.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Man | Woman | Both
Exhibitions should be different and diverse = Man
Traditional customs are gradually losing their significance = Both
Local festivals will disappear in the near future = Woman
Schools are important in shaping future generations = Woman

mk1-lt5-p4a.audio:
AUDIO: audio/t5_q16.mp3
W: The biggest gap right now is that we haven't adequately explored the characters' backstories through their dialogue. Market demand and tight broadcast deadlines are pushing us to rush through the script development cycle. When you cut corners on editing and refinement, the final quality of the project takes a hit.
mk1-lt5-p4a.title: Bài nói 1
mk1-lt5-p4a.instr: Listen to a TV producer sharing his thoughts on the latest scripts for a new show.
mk1-lt5-p4a.body:
What does the producer think about the dialogues in the new show?
*The characters' backgrounds are not adequately explored
They seem unrealistic.
They reflect real-life conversations well.

How is the current industry demand affecting the quality of script production?
It is allowing for more thorough script development.
It is leading to more innovative ideas.
*It is negatively influencing script production.

mk1-lt5-p4b.audio:
AUDIO: audio/t5_q17.mp3
W: While the food itself was decent, the real issue lies with the service. From the moment I arrived, it was clear that the staff were either overwhelmed or under-trained. What can compete with the ease of ordering from home is the feeling of being truly valued and welcomed.
mk1-lt5-p4b.title: Bài nói 2
mk1-lt5-p4b.instr: Listen to a critic giving opinions about a restaurant.
mk1-lt5-p4b.body:
What are the critic's opinions about the restaurant?
The food is not fresh
*The service is not good
The chef lacks experience

What can compete with online food delivery?
Organic ingredients
Providing a ready-made pack for customers
*Customers feel valued and welcome

mk2-lt4-p1.title: Nghe và chọn chi tiết
mk2-lt4-p1.instr: Nghe từng đoạn và chọn đáp án đúng. Mỗi đoạn được nghe tối đa 2 lần.
mk2-lt4-p1.body:
A man is calling his friend, Maria. When will he see her?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q1.mp3
W: Hey Maria, it's me! I wanted to let you know that I'll be visiting your town this weekend. But the best part? I'll finally get to see you! I'll be at your place at 9 a.m. on Sunday, so we can catch up. Can't wait to hang out!
*at 9 am on Sunday
at 10 am on Saturday
at 8 am on Sunday

A man is calling his colleague about a meeting with clients. When will the meeting start?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q2.mp3
W: Hey, just wanted to give you a quick heads-up. I won't be able to join the meeting with the clients at 10:15 like we planned - I've got something that suddenly came up. Could you go ahead and handle the presentation on your own?
at 9.15
*at 10.15
at 11.15

A customer is calling the hotline of a department store. Which number to press in order to buy a computer?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q3.mp3
W: Thank you for calling our customer service hotline. To file a complaint about a recent purchase, please press 1. For assistance with maintenance or repairs, press 2. If you'd like a free consultation on buying a new computer, press 3.
One
Two
*Three

An expert is talking about the lack of satisfaction at work. What should be the solution?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q4.mp3
W: Many people feel unhappy at work, and often, they think a higher salary or less work will fix it. But that's not always the solution. One option is to ask for a transfer to another branch within the same company. This can offer the same benefits as getting a new job, without the challenges of starting over somewhere new.
Raise the salary
Seek a new job
*Request a transfer

A man is talking to his friend. Why does he need to learn to drive?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q5.mp3
M: I'm moving to a new place. It's actually pretty far from my workplace, and the public transport there isn't great. So, I've been thinking, I need to learn how to drive.
W: That makes sense.
He lost his driving license.
*He has to drive to work
He bought a new car.

A tour guide is talking about birds' behaviors. What do birds do in the winter?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q6.mp3
W: In spring, birds are busy building nests and finding mates. During summer, they're focused on feeding their chicks. As autumn approaches, many birds begin to migrate. In winter, birds tend to stay together in groups for protection from predators.
*Stay together for group protection
Building nests
Migrate to a new place

Two friends are talking about their school days. What was the woman good at?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q7.mp3
M: You were on the football team, right?
W: Yeah, I played for the school team. Those were some of my best memories!
M: I wasn't great at football, but I was pretty good at swimming.
W: Swimming was totally your strength. Just like football was mine.
Swimming
*Plays football
Running

Pierre and Emma are talking together about the picnic on the weekend. What will they bring to the picnic?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q8.mp3
W: Emma: So, what should we bring? Maybe some food in case we might get hungry? Pierre: That's a good idea. How about we prepare some chicken and french fries? Emma: Perfect! This picnic is going to be amazing!
Drinks
Salads
*Food

A tour guide is talking about the group's traveling schedule. Where will the group wait for the bus?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q9.mp3
W: Finally, at 8:00 PM, we'll meet at the hotel's main entrance to catch the bus to the airport. Make sure to be on time, and we'll head to the airport together!
by the hotel's side entrance
behind the hotel's main entrance
*by the hotel's main entrance

Listen to the announcement from a travel agent representative. Why is the air travel cancelled?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q10.mp3
W: Unfortunately, due to poor weather conditions, our flight has been cancelled. I know this isn't the news you were hoping for, but your safety comes first. That said, we do have alternatives available - trains and buses are still running.
Engine failure
*Poor weather conditions
Delay at transit spot

A saleswoman is talking to a customer about a house. What is not original?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q11.mp3
W: The hardwood floors you see here are completely original. The same goes for the architecture - those high ceilings and detailed moldings are a testament to the craftsmanship of that era. However, the furniture you see isn't original. It was replaced a few years ago.
Floor
*Furniture
Architecture

Listen to a weather forecast. Where will the weather be best?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q12.mp3
W: The weather down south isn't looking too great - strong winds and heavy rain. The west will have decent weather with clear skies and mild temperatures. However, the best weather can be found in the east, where we're expecting sunny skies and perfect temperatures.
In the south
In the west
*In the east

Adam is calling his friend. When will he need the computer?
AUDIO: audio/t4_q13.mp3
W: Hey James, it's Adam! I'm happy to let you borrow mine on Tuesday. Just make sure to take good care of it! But I need it back by Friday because I have a group presentation on Saturday.
Tuesday
*Friday
Saturday

mk2-lt4-p2.title: Ghép người nói
mk2-lt4-p2.instr: Four people are talking about doing arts. Match each speaker with what they say.
mk2-lt4-p2.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Doing as a social activity | Doing arts with children | Doing arts as part of the job | Doing arts alone
Speaker A = Doing as a social activity
AUDIO: audio/t4_q14_1.mp3
W: I love when people come together to create something - it's not just about the art itself but about connecting with each other. Ideas bounce around, and suddenly, new ones come to life. Art becomes a shared experience, bringing us all together.
Speaker B = Doing arts with children
AUDIO: audio/t4_q14_2.mp3
W: Kids are so fearless with art. They jump in, without worrying about mistakes, making everything feel magical. Teaching them is a reminder that creativity should be free and fun.
Speaker C = Doing arts as part of the job
AUDIO: audio/t4_q14_3.mp3
W: Art is part of my work, so it comes with structure - deadlines, clients, and goals. It's different from personal art because I'm balancing my ideas with what's needed for the project. But there's a thrill in that challenge.
Speaker D = Doing arts alone
AUDIO: audio/t4_q14_4.mp3
W: Art, for me, is a quiet, personal thing. It's my time to focus inward, away from distractions. I don't need anyone else there, it's just me and my thoughts. Creating alone brings a peace where I can explore and express freely.

mk2-lt4-p3.audio:
AUDIO: audio/t4_q15.mp3
M: Urban farming will take up land that could be used for accommodation.
W: Unused spaces that are too small for housing can be converted into farming areas. If done right, this could be both beneficial and visually attractive.
M: Rural farming is still a more practical option.
W: That's true, and I agree. But changes need to happen.
mk2-lt4-p3.title: Ai có ý kiến này?
mk2-lt4-p3.instr: A man and a woman are talking about urban farming. Decide whose opinion matches each statement: the man, the woman, or both. You can listen twice.
mk2-lt4-p3.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Man | Woman | Both
Living space is more important than farming space = Man
Farming space is appealing = Woman
Farming space will benefit the urban economy = Woman
Farming space is in need of more food = Both

mk2-lt4-p4a.audio:
AUDIO: audio/t4_q16.mp3
W: A famous TV series called Mystery City was recently broadcasted, and it caught the audience's attention from the start. Beyond just entertaining, Mystery City has also helped its network reach new customers. The show attracted a diverse audience, including younger viewers.
mk2-lt4-p4a.title: Bài nói 1
mk2-lt4-p4a.instr: Listen to a critic talking about a newly broadcast TV series.
mk2-lt4-p4a.body:
What happened to the TV series?
It didn't receive enough investment in the early stage.
It was overlooked by critics.
*It caught the audience's attention from the start.

According to the expert, what is the series' potential?
New seasons will be produced due to great demand.
It inspires young filmmakers to follow a new movie-making style.
*It can help reach new customers.

mk2-lt4-p4b.audio:
AUDIO: audio/t4_q17.mp3
W: Many TV series have been damaged by overexposure. In terms of sports, overexposure can generate negative publicity for the sport itself. Fans may start to associate their favorite teams and players with annoying advertisements rather than the thrilling action on the field.
mk2-lt4-p4b.title: Bài nói 2
mk2-lt4-p4b.instr: Listen to an advertising expert talking about the advertising industry.
mk2-lt4-p4b.body:
What does the expert say about the negative side of advertising?
*Series are damaged by overexposure.
Advertisements might sometimes be repetitive, which is annoying.
Advertising costs the same amount of money to produce a movie.

In what way can advertising affect sports?
They help to attract more fans.
They can boost ticket sales and sales of sports-related items.
*They can generate negative publicity for the sport.

mk1-wc-social-club-p1.title: Trả lời tin nhắn ngắn
mk1-wc-social-club-p1.instr: Trả lời mỗi tin nhắn bằng 1–5 từ. Nên xong trong khoảng 3 phút.
mk1-wc-social-club-p1.body:
CÂU HỎI: What's the weather like today?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Mẫu 1: The weather today is sunny and warm, which makes me feel relaxed.
Mẫu 2: It is sunny today.

CÂU HỎI: How are you?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Mẫu 1: I am doing well today, thank you for asking.
Mẫu 2: I am fine, thank you.

CÂU HỎI: What's your hobby?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Mẫu 1: I enjoy reading books and hiking in nature in my free time.
Mẫu 2: I enjoy listening to music.

CÂU HỎI: How do you get to work?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Mẫu 1: I get to work by driving my bike because it is more convenient for me.
Mẫu 2: I usually walk to work.

CÂU HỎI: What do you like to do in the evening?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Mẫu 1: In the evening, I usually relax by reading a good book or listening to music.
Mẫu 2: I like listening to music.

mk1-wc-social-club-p2.title: Viết đoạn ngắn
mk1-wc-social-club-p2.instr: Trả lời bằng câu hoàn chỉnh, 20–30 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 7 phút.
mk1-wc-social-club-p2.body:
CÂU HỎI: What do you like to do with friends and where do you go?
SỐ TỪ: 20-30
BÀI MẪU: I enjoy going out for coffee with my friends. I like it because we can talk and relax together. For example, we often visit a cosy café on Sundays.

mk1-wc-social-club-p3.title: Trả lời nhóm chat
mk1-wc-social-club-p3.instr: Trả lời các thành viên trong nhóm chat, mỗi câu 30–40 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 10 phút.
mk1-wc-social-club-p3.body:
CÂU HỎI: Where did you meet your friends for the first time and how did you become friends?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! I first met my best friends in an English class two years ago. We became close because we did a group project together. After that, we started meeting outside class for coffee and long conversations.

CÂU HỎI: I have just moved to the city and want to make some friends. Can you give me some advice?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! Welcome to the city! I suggest joining a local club or social group. I recommend this because it is the easiest way to meet people. For example, you could join a sports team or a book club at weekends.

CÂU HỎI: Some people say we should share our hobbies with our friends, do you agree with this and why?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! Yes, I totally agree that we should share our hobbies with friends. I think so because it makes friendships stronger and more fun. For example, my friends and I play badminton together every weekend.

CÂU HỎI: It is much easier to make new friends these days because of computers and mobile phones. Do you agree? Why or why not?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! I don't really agree with this idea. I think so because people now chat online instead of meeting face to face. I also believe real friendships need time together, not just messages on a phone.

mk1-wc-social-club-p4.title: Viết 2 email
mk1-wc-social-club-p4.instr: Email cho bạn khoảng 50 từ (thân mật) và email cho quản lý 120–150 từ (trang trọng). Khoảng 30 phút.
mk1-wc-social-club-p4.body:
CÂU HỎI: Write to a friend about the club's online/offline event idea
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi John,
I'm really excited about the club's idea of monthly meetings.
I think it would be great to meet in places that are easy to reach by bus.
I'm considering suggesting both weekend and weekday evening meetings.
What do you think?
Talk soon,
Viet Anh

CÂU HỎI: Write to a friend about the club's monthly face-to-face meeting idea
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi Ha,
I'm really excited about the club's plan for face-to-face meetings.
I think it would be great to meet on Sunday mornings because we're busy during the week.
I'm considering suggesting a local café.
What do you think?
Talk soon,
Anh Hao

CÂU HỎI: Write to the club manager about the online/offline event idea
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about whether our monthly meetings should be held online or in person. I am very pleased that the club wants members to meet more regularly.
I would like to suggest holding the meetings face to face. I believe this would be more effective because people communicate more naturally and build stronger friendships in person. However, some members live far away or have busy schedules, so they may find it difficult to attend.
If a face-to-face meeting is not possible every month, we could hold an online meeting every second month instead. I also suggest choosing places that are easy to reach by public transport and alternating between weekends and weekday evenings, so that everyone has a chance to join.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Nguyen Viet Anh

CÂU HỎI: Write to the club manager about when/where to hold monthly meetings
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about when and where to hold our monthly face-to-face meetings. I am very pleased about this plan, as it is a great chance for members to make new friends.
I would like to suggest meeting on Sunday mornings at a quiet café. I believe this is the best choice because younger members are busy with work and classes during the week, while older members prefer a relaxed morning. However, popular cafés can be crowded at the weekend.
If a café is unavailable, we could use a meeting room at the local community centre. I also suggest booking the venue a month in advance, so that members can plan their schedules and the club can avoid last-minute problems.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Anh Hao

mk2-wc-language-club-p1.title: Trả lời tin nhắn ngắn
mk2-wc-language-club-p1.instr: Trả lời mỗi tin nhắn bằng 1–5 từ. Nên xong trong khoảng 3 phút.

SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: It is raining heavily today. / It is quite hot and sunny today.

CÂU HỎI: What do you do in your free time?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: I usually listen to music.

CÂU HỎI: What is your first language?

BÀI MẪU: My mother tongue is Vietnamese.

CÂU HỎI: Who do you usually go to the movies with?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: I normally go with my girlfriend.

CÂU HỎI: What food do you like?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5

CÂU HỎI: How often do you go for a walk?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: I usually go for a walk in the park every evening after work.

CÂU HỎI: What do you do in the evening?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: In the evening, I often read books or listen to music to relax.

CÂU HỎI: Where are you going to tomorrow?

BÀI MẪU: Tomorrow, I am going to attend a training workshop with my colleagues.

mk2-wc-language-club-p2.title: Viết đoạn ngắn
mk2-wc-language-club-p2.instr: Trả lời bằng câu hoàn chỉnh, 20–30 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 7 phút.
mk2-wc-language-club-p2.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me your free time and interests?
SỐ TỪ: 20-30
BÀI MẪU: In my free time, I usually play football with friends. I enjoy it because it keeps me healthy. Also, I like listening to music to relax after work.

CÂU HỎI: In which cases do you often use foreign languages?
SỐ TỪ: 20-30
BÀI MẪU: I mainly use English at work. I need it because I communicate with international clients. For example, I write emails and join online meetings in English every week.

CÂU HỎI: Where do you usually study and why?
SỐ TỪ: 20-30
BÀI MẪU: I usually study at a quiet coffee shop near my apartment. I go there because the atmosphere is peaceful. For example, I can focus for hours without any distractions.

mk2-wc-language-club-p3.title: Trả lời nhóm chat
mk2-wc-language-club-p3.instr: Trả lời các thành viên trong nhóm chat, mỗi câu 30–40 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 10 phút.
mk2-wc-language-club-p3.body:
CÂU HỎI: Why did you choose this course?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! I chose this course to improve my English communication skills. I need them because I use English in meetings at work. I also hope it will help me find better job opportunities in the future.

CÂU HỎI: How have you found the course so far? What's been difficult?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! So far, I have really enjoyed the course. I like it because the lessons are interesting and easy to follow. However, listening is still difficult for me because native speakers often talk very quickly.

CÂU HỎI: What are you hoping to do when you finish the course?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! After the course, I hope to use English more naturally at work and when I travel. I want this because it will make me more confident. I also plan to take an English certificate to improve my CV.

CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a memory you have with a foreign language?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! I still remember the first time I spoke English with a foreign customer. I was nervous because my English was not perfect. However, the customer was very friendly, and I felt much more confident afterwards.

CÂU HỎI: I am very forgetful. Can you give me tips to remember new words?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! I suggest using each new word in a sentence straight away. I recommend this because using words helps you remember them longer. For example, you can write three sentences with new words every evening.

CÂU HỎI: What do you think is the most effective way to learn English?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! I think the most effective way is to practise a little every day. I believe this because regular practice is better than studying a lot at once. For example, you can watch short videos and speak with friends daily.

CÂU HỎI: Do you remember anything about foreign language classes in school?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! Yes, I remember my English classes at high school very clearly. I enjoyed them because my teacher organised fun group discussions. I also became more confident in speaking thanks to those interesting activities.

CÂU HỎI: Why is learning a new language important?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi! I think learning a new language is very important. I believe this because it helps us communicate with people from different cultures. I also think it creates better study and career opportunities in today's world.

mk2-wc-language-club-p4.title: Viết 2 email
mk2-wc-language-club-p4.instr: Email cho bạn khoảng 50 từ (thân mật) và email cho quản lý 120–150 từ (trang trọng). Khoảng 30 phút.
mk2-wc-language-club-p4.body:
CÂU HỎI: Write to a friend about new features for the club website
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi Ngan,
I'm really excited about the new features planned for the club website.
I think it would be great to add online chat rooms and vocabulary games.
I'm considering sending these ideas to the manager this week.
What do you think?
Talk soon,
Anh

CÂU HỎI: Write to a friend recommending the English course you're taking
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi Ngan,
I'm really pleased with the English course I'm taking at American Dream Center.
I think it would be great for you too, because my speaking has improved a lot.
I'm considering asking if we could join a class together.
What do you think?
Hugs,
Anh

CÂU HỎI: Write to the club manager explaining why you can't continue the course
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about my English course at A Level Speaking Center. I am very pleased with the lessons, but I am sorry to say that I cannot continue for the next few weeks.
I would like to suggest pausing my course temporarily. I believe this is the best solution because I have just started a new full-time job and my schedule is very busy at the moment. However, I do not want to lose my place, as the teachers have been very supportive.
If pausing the course is not possible, we could move me to an evening or weekend class that fits my working hours. I also suggest sending me the lesson materials online, so that I can keep studying at home until I return.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Nguyen Quoc Anh

CÂU HỎI: Write to a friend about applying to be a guest speaker
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi Ngan,
I'm really excited that the club is looking for a guest speaker.
I think it would be great to talk about practical ways to improve English.
I'm considering applying for the role this week.
Do you think it's a good idea?
Talk soon,
Anh

CÂU HỎI: Write to the club expressing your desire to be a guest speaker
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about the club's search for a speaker for the upcoming lecture. I am very excited about this event, and I would like to apply to be the speaker.
I would like to suggest a talk on how to use English effectively in daily life and at work. I believe I am suitable for this role because I have given similar presentations many times and I enjoy sharing practical tips. However, I understand that other members may also want to apply.
If the main lecture is unavailable, we could organise a shorter workshop where I share my ideas with a smaller group. I also suggest including a question-and-answer session at the end, so that members can ask about their own learning problems.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Nguyen Quoc Anh

CÂU HỎI: Write to the club manager about new website features
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about the new features planned for the club website. I am very pleased that the club wants to make the website more useful for its members.
I would like to suggest adding online discussion rooms where members can practise speaking together. I believe this would be very effective because learners need regular practice with real people to become confident. However, discussion rooms need someone to manage them, which may take a lot of time.
If a full-time moderator is unavailable, we could ask experienced members to take turns managing the rooms each week. I also suggest adding vocabulary quizzes and daily reminders, so that members are encouraged to study a little every day.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Thao Van Truong

mk1-sp1-02.title: Bộ 2
mk1-sp1-02.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
mk1-sp1-02.body:
CÂU HỎI: What do you like doing with your friends? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I always prioritise spending my downtime with my friends; it's essential for me. While we enjoy a lot of activities - like catching a film or hitting a concert occasionally - I'm particularly keen on simply hanging out at a local coffee shop. We usually grab some great drinks, like green tea or a good espresso, and it’s the perfect setting to catch up on exciting news and share anecdotes. It’s just great quality time and it helps me recharge my batteries socially.
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about one of your good memories | 30
BÀI MẪU: One memory that stands out vividly for me is the day I successfully completed my first major marathon. It was a huge personal challenge. I remember the incredible feeling of elation and relief crossing the finish line, especially since I had been training rigorously for months. The cheering crowds and the sight of my family waiting there made the whole experience absolutely unforgettable. It truly taught me the value of perseverance.
CÂU HỎI: What is the weather like today? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Well, the weather in Hanoi today is absolutely delightful - it’s quintessential autumn. It’s pleasantly cool, with the temperature hovering around 18 to 20 degrees Celsius. The sky is largely clear, but there’s a slight, gentle breeze which makes it feel a bit crisp. This is my favourite kind of weather, actually, as it’s perfect for taking a leisurely walk outside without feeling too cold. All in all, it’s a beautifully mild day.

mk1-sp2-01.part: Part 2 · Describe, express opinion, give reasons
mk1-sp2-01.title: Bộ 1
mk1-sp2-01.instr: Mô tả bức ảnh rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Ảnh của đề không kèm theo; xem câu trả lời mẫu để biết nội dung ảnh.
mk1-sp2-01.body:
CÂU HỎI: Describe the picture | 45
BÀI MẪU: This is the first time I have seen such an awesome picture as the one on the screen. When I first look at it, I can see a family of three: a dad, a mom, and their daughter.
The dad is sitting at the dining table; he appears to be around 35 years old with a thick beard. It seems like he is having breakfast, and there is a glass of orange juice on the table. The mom looks to be about 30 years old, with a beautiful face, a shining smile, and curly blonde hair. She is holding a book, seemingly reading a story to her little daughter, who is lying in her lap listening. The girl looks to be around 10 years old, with a bright face, and she is intently focused on her mom’s storytelling.
Besides, it’s not difficult to see that they are in their cozy home, with everything neatly arranged and plenty of space for sunlight to come in. The picture reminds me of my own family when I was a child. Back then, I lived close to my parents and enjoyed spending weekends together. Now, I have moved to the city for work and can only be with my family during major holidays.
CÂU HỎI: Why is it important to play with children? | 45
BÀI MẪU: Playing with children is undeniably important. I believe it is crucial for parents and children to spend quality time together because it helps build a natural, healthy, and emotional bond that can last a lifetime. When parents and children engage in activities together, it also creates beautiful and lasting memories. Moreover, spending time together teaches children how to interact with others by developing their respect and empathy. Finally, it allows parents to guide and discipline their children if needed, which is essential for helping them grow into responsible and good citizens in the future.
CÂU HỎI: How should parents spend time together with their children? | 45
BÀI MẪU: Parents should spend time with their children both outdoors and indoors. Outdoor activities can include playing sports like badminton or tennis, going for a walk, or having a picnic. Indoor activities might involve playing puzzles, watching TV, or reading books together.
In Vietnam, parents are often busy during the day, but they try to spend time with their kids in the evenings. That’s why families usually have dinner together, which provides a great opportunity to connect and share their day. Additionally, parents often help their children with homework, study English, or learn other subjects, which supports their children's education and development.

mk1-sp3-01.title: Bộ 1
mk1-sp3-01.instr: Mô tả và so sánh hai bức ảnh, rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Ảnh của đề không kèm theo; xem câu trả lời mẫu để biết nội dung ảnh.
mk1-sp3-01.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me what you see from the two pictures? | 45
BÀI MẪU: Wow, actually these two pictures are really interesting, and both of them are related to how families spend their leisure time together. When I look at the first picture, it’s quite easy to see a mother and her daughter playing a video game together. They seem to be in their living room, sitting comfortably on a sofa. Both of them look very happy and energetic. While the first picture feels lively and modern, the second picture shows a family playing a traditional game of chess around a table. The atmosphere here appears much calmer and more relaxed, and they seem to be enjoying a quiet moment of face-to-face interaction. Personally, I prefer the second one because it encourages closer family bonding without technology.
CÂU HỎI: Compare the two activities. Which one do you think is more suitable? | 45
BÀI MẪU: In my opinion, both activities help children develop different skills, but I personally find playing chess more suitable. Playing video games helps children become familiar with technology and develop quick reactions and hand-eye coordination. However, chess requires much deeper thinking. Players need to observe carefully, be patient, and predict their opponent’s moves in order to build an effective strategy. Personally, I prefer playing chess because it helps me improve my perseverance, my ability to analyse situations, and my skill in finding solutions. These qualities are extremely useful and can be applied a lot in my own work.
CÂU HỎI: Do you think playing computer games is good for children? Why or why not? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I believe playing computer games can be good for children if it is properly controlled. On the positive side, some educational or strategic games can improve problem-solving skills, creativity, and hand-eye coordination. They can also help children relax after studying. However, if children spend too much time playing computer games, it may negatively affect their health, concentration, and social skills. Therefore, I think computer games are beneficial only when children play them in moderation and with guidance from parents.

mk1-sp4n-03.title: 3. A time you were in a hurry
mk1-sp4n-03.instr: Kể lần vội vàng, bận rộn; nêu quan điểm về cuộc sống hiện đại bận rộn. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
mk1-sp4n-03.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me a time when you were in a hurry.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about a time when I was in a hurry.
It happened a few months ago. I had an important meeting at work in the morning, but I woke up late.
I quickly got dressed, had a simple breakfast and went to work as fast as possible.
Unfortunately, there was a lot of traffic on the road, so I was quite worried about being late.
Luckily, I arrived just a few minutes before the meeting started.
**Since then, I have tried to prepare everything the night before and wake up earlier.**
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel?
BÀI MẪU: I felt very stressed and worried because I didn't want to be late for the meeting.
I also realized that rushing can make people forget important things.
After that experience, I learned that good preparation can save a lot of time.
CÂU HỎI: Modern life makes us busier and more rushed. What do you think?
BÀI MẪU: Yes, I agree with this idea.
Nowadays, people have many responsibilities. They have to work, study, take care of their families and deal with many messages and emails.
Technology makes our lives more convenient, but sometimes it also makes us feel that we always have to be available.
**I think people should manage their time carefully and make time for rest.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: wake up late | meeting | traffic | stressed | preparation | responsibilities | technology | rest

mk2-sp1-05.title: Bộ 5
mk2-sp1-05.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
mk2-sp1-05.body:
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about your family? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I live in a nuclear family with my parents and my older brother. My father is a dedicated farmer in the countryside, whereas my mother is a full-time homemaker. My brother, who is a qualified engineer, and I both work as office professionals in the city. Consequently, we only manage to reunite during major national holidays, such as Tết or National Day. Despite the distance, we remain extremely close-knit and cherish those precious gatherings.
CÂU HỎI: Describe your favorite places? | 30
BÀI MẪU: While there are many places I enjoy, Nha Trang is undoubtedly my top destination. I genuinely believe it's one of the most stunning coastal cities in Vietnam, thanks to its pristine beaches and clear water. I always look forward to spending an extended break there because it offers the perfect opportunity to unwind completely, indulge in fresh seafood, and partake in various water sports. Ultimately, Nha Trang is the ideal spot to recharge and find new inspiration.
CÂU HỎI: What do you like to do in your free time? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I have always considered myself an avid movie enthusiast, so naturally, my favourite way to spend my downtime is binge-watching different series on platforms like Netflix. I find it the perfect activity to unwind completely after a demanding schedule. For me, getting immersed in a compelling storyline is not just entertainment; it’s genuinely the most effective way to switch off from reality and recharge my batteries both mentally and emotionally.

mk2-sp2-03.part: Part 2 · Describe, express opinion, give reasons
mk2-sp2-03.title: Bộ 3
mk2-sp2-03.instr: Mô tả bức ảnh rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Ảnh của đề không kèm theo; xem câu trả lời mẫu để biết nội dung ảnh.
mk2-sp2-03.body:
CÂU HỎI: Describe the picture | 45
BÀI MẪU: This is the first time I have seen such an awesome picture as I can see on the screen. When I first look at this, I can see a teacher standing at the front of a classroom, teaching a group of students who are sitting and facing her.
She’s about 30 years old with a beautiful face, a warm, shining smile, and dark hair. She’s wearing a light yellow cardigan over a white top, paired with a dark skirt. It’s not difficult to see that she’s in a classroom because I can see students sitting at desks, with notebooks and other school supplies in front of them. She seems to be on top of the world as she’s confidently engaging with her students, possibly explaining a lesson or guiding them through an activity.
The picture reminds me of my own school days, particularly a favorite teacher who always made learning enjoyable, just like the woman in the picture.
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about the last time you studied something in class | 45
BÀI MẪU: The last time I studied something in class was just yesterday. I attended a physics lecture with my university classmates, and it was taught by my favorite professor, Ms. Lee. I found the lesson particularly engaging because Ms. Lee used real-world examples to explain the concept of gravity. She even conducted some practical demonstrations, which really helped to bring the theory to life. It made the topic much more comprehensible and enjoyable for me.
CÂU HỎI: How can teachers make the lessons interesting? | 45
BÀI MẪU: In my point of view, teachers can make lessons more interesting in a few key ways. One effective approach is to incorporate interactive activities, such as mini games with small rewards, which can capture students' attention and make learning more enjoyable. Another strategy is to integrate multimedia elements like videos or images, which can enhance the lesson by providing visual and auditory stimulation, making the material more engaging. Additionally, linking the content to real-world examples or current events can help students understand the relevance of the lesson, keeping them more motivated and invested in the subject matter.

mk2-sp3-04.title: Bộ 4
mk2-sp3-04.instr: Mô tả và so sánh hai bức ảnh, rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Ảnh của đề không kèm theo; xem câu trả lời mẫu để biết nội dung ảnh.
mk2-sp3-04.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell me what you see in the two pictures? | 45
BÀI MẪU: Wow, these two pictures are really captivating, and they make me want to dive right into describing them. In my view, both pictures depict children engaged in play, but in very different environments and activities.
In the first picture, it’s easy to see three children playing with toys indoors. They appear to be having a good time in what looks like a cozy, comfortable space, possibly a living room or a playroom. The toys are scattered around, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The children seem focused and happy, fully immersed in their play.
The second picture, however, contrasts sharply with the first. In this image, I can see a group of children playing outside, hula hooping in the sunlight. The setting is outdoors, surrounded by greenery with trees and grass, giving the scene a fresh, vibrant feel. The bright sunlight adds energy to the scene, and the children seem to be thoroughly enjoying the physical activity and the fresh air.
Both pictures beautifully capture the essence of play, but they do so in different contexts—one indoors with toys, and the other outdoors with hula hoops, highlighting the diversity of how children can enjoy themselves.
CÂU HỎI: How do children benefit from spending time in these ways? | 45
BÀI MẪU: Well, I believe that both activities are highly beneficial for children. They help children relax and alleviate stress, which is crucial for their overall well-being. Additionally, these activities are good for children's health, promoting physical fitness and mental stimulation. Furthermore, when children engage in these activities, they have the opportunity to make new friends, which is important for their social development and confidence.
CÂU HỎI: Why is it important for children to play together? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I believe playing together is essential for children for several reasons. Firstly, it makes the experience more enjoyable and fun for them. Secondly, it provides an excellent opportunity for children to easily make friends and build social connections. Playing together also helps them develop important social skills, such as teamwork and communication, which are crucial for their overall development.

mk2-sp4n-08.title: 8. Extreme sport
mk2-sp4n-08.instr: Kể lần chơi hoặc xem người khác chơi thể thao mạo hiểm; nêu quan điểm có nên cho trẻ em chơi không. Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu. Từ khóa gợi ý nằm ở mục Cụm từ hữu ích.
mk2-sp4n-08.body:
CÂU HỎI: Tell a time you did or saw someone do an extreme sport.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about a time when I tried an adventurous activity with my friends.
It happened during a trip. We decided to go hiking on a fairly difficult mountain trail.
The trail was quite steep in some places, so we had to be very careful.
At first, I was a little scared because I wasn't used to this kind of activity.
However, my friends encouraged me, and I continued.
When we reached the top, I felt extremely happy and excited.
**It was challenging but also a very memorable experience.**
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel?
BÀI MẪU: At first, I felt nervous because the activity was quite difficult.
But after I got used to it, I started to enjoy the experience.
When I reached the top, I felt proud because I had overcome my fear.
CÂU HỎI: Should adults allow children to play extreme sports?
BÀI MẪU: I think it depends on the type of sport and the age of the child.
Extreme sports can help children become more confident and physically active.
However, safety should always come first.
Adults should choose suitable activities and make sure children have proper equipment and supervision.
**So, I don't think children should be completely prevented from trying adventurous activities, but they need to be carefully controlled.**
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CỤM TỪ: adventure | hiking | difficult | steep | nervous | overcome fear | safety | supervision

Running is one of the easiest ways to get fit, but many beginners give up too soon.
The most common mistake is trying to run too far in the first week.
Instead, start with short sessions of walking and jogging.
For example, you could jog for one minute and then walk for two.
Over time, you can increase the jogging and reduce the walking.
After about two months, most people can run for thirty minutes without stopping.

mk3-r3.intro:
Linh: When my company let us work from home, I was delighted. I no longer spend two hours a day in traffic, and I use that time to exercise. The downside is that I sometimes forget to stop working – my laptop is always there on the kitchen table.

Daniel: I tried working from home for a year and I hated it. I live alone, so I went days without speaking to anyone. Now I go to the office every day, even though it's optional. I need people around me to stay motivated.

Mai: For me, the best solution is a mix. I do focused tasks like writing reports at home, and I go in for meetings and team projects. My manager trusts us to choose, which I really appreciate.

Robert: As a manager, I have mixed feelings. My team is more productive at home, according to our figures, but it's harder to train new staff. Young employees learn a lot just by listening to experienced colleagues, and that doesn't happen on video calls.

mk3-r4.title: Ghép tiêu đề: làm việc từ xa
mk3-r4.instr: Bài đọc dài khoảng 750 từ như đề thật. Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Có 8 tiêu đề cho 7 đoạn, một tiêu đề thừa.
mk3-r4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: A change that happened overnight | Cities feel the effect | Not everyone can stay at home | Rethinking the office | Saving time and money | The end of the office forever | The hidden costs for workers | Trust between managers and staff
Before 2020, working from home was a privilege enjoyed by a small number of employees, usually senior staff or freelancers. Most companies believed that people needed to be in the office to work properly, and many managers were openly suspicious of anyone who asked to work remotely. Then, almost overnight, the pandemic forced millions of people to set up desks in their bedrooms and kitchens. Technology that had existed for years, such as video calls and shared online documents, suddenly became part of everyday life. Within a few weeks, companies that had insisted remote work was impossible discovered that much of their business could continue without anyone entering the building. For many workers, it was the biggest change to their working lives they had ever experienced, and it happened without any planning at all. = A change that happened overnight
For many employees, the most obvious benefit was the end of the daily commute. Office workers in large cities often spend more than an hour travelling each way, and that time could now be used for sleep, exercise or family. Commuting is also expensive. Train tickets, petrol, parking and lunches bought near the office can add up to a significant part of a monthly salary. Surveys carried out in several countries found that people working from home saved, on average, several thousand dollars a year. Some even decided to move to cheaper areas far from the city, knowing they would rarely need to travel to work. For young families, the extra flexibility meant that parents could take children to school and still start work on time. = Saving time and money
However, the experience was not positive for everyone. Workers living in small flats often had no quiet place to work, and many ended up sitting on the sofa or the bed for hours, which caused back and neck problems. Electricity and heating bills went up, and few employers offered to help with these costs. Others found that the line between work and home disappeared completely. When your office is also your living room, it is tempting to check emails late at night or at weekends. Psychologists reported a rise in stress and exhaustion among people who felt they were always available. Loneliness was another common complaint, particularly among those who lived alone and missed the casual conversations of office life. = The hidden costs for workers
It is also important to remember that remote work was only ever an option for certain jobs. Nurses, shop assistants, factory workers, cleaners and delivery drivers continued to travel to work throughout the pandemic, often facing greater risks than those who could stay at home. This created a new kind of inequality. Generally, people in well-paid office jobs gained flexibility and savings, while many of those in lower-paid roles gained nothing. Some experts warned that this gap could create resentment within society, especially when politicians and business leaders talked about remote work as if it were available to everyone. = Not everyone can stay at home
One of the most interesting changes was in the relationship between managers and employees. Traditionally, many managers judged their staff by how many hours they spent at their desks. When they could no longer see their teams, they had to start measuring results instead. Some found this difficult and introduced software to track what employees were doing on their computers, which caused anger and damaged morale. Others discovered that when people were given more freedom, they often worked harder and were more loyal to the company. Studies suggest that organisations which trusted their staff during this period kept more of them in the following years. = Trust between managers and staff
The shift has also affected cities themselves. With fewer people travelling to business districts, cafés, sandwich shops and dry cleaners that depended on office workers lost much of their income, and some closed permanently. Public transport companies saw passenger numbers fall dramatically. At the same time, smaller towns and suburbs became busier, as people spent more money close to where they lived. City councils are now considering how to bring life back to central areas, for example by turning empty office blocks into apartments, which could also help to reduce housing shortages. = Cities feel the effect
So what does the future hold for the office? Few experts believe it will disappear completely. Instead, many companies are adopting a hybrid model, where staff spend part of the week at home and part in the office. Offices themselves are being redesigned, with fewer individual desks and more spaces for meetings, teamwork and social events. The idea is that people will come in to collaborate, to learn from one another and to build relationships, and do their quieter, focused work at home. Whether this balance will last is still uncertain, but it seems clear that the traditional five-day week in the office is unlikely to return for many workers. = Rethinking the office

mk3-lp4b.audio: M: Parents often ask me how to make their child a professional footballer. My answer usually surprises them. I tell them to let their children play lots of different sports until they're at least twelve. Children who only play football from the age of five often get injured, and many of them lose interest before they're teenagers. Playing tennis, swimming or basketball develops balance and coordination in ways football alone doesn't. Of course, talent matters, but in my experience, the players who make it are the ones who still love the game at eighteen. My job is to protect that enjoyment, not to win every match in the under-tens league.
mk3-lp4b.title: Bài nói 2
mk3-lp4b.instr: Listen to a football coach talking about training young players. Answer two questions.
mk3-lp4b.body:
What advice does the coach give parents?
*Children should try a variety of sports
Children should start football as early as possible
Children should focus on one sport
? "let their children play lots of different sports until they're at least twelve".

What does the coach believe is most important?
*Keeping young players' enjoyment of the game
Winning matches in youth leagues
Finding talented players early
? "My job is to protect that enjoyment, not to win every match".

SỐ TỪ: 1-5

SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Around seven o'clock.

CÂU HỎI: Where do you buy food?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: At a local market.

CÂU HỎI: What did you eat for breakfast?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5

mk3-w2.title: Viết đoạn ngắn
mk3-w2.instr: Trả lời bằng câu hoàn chỉnh, 20–30 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 7 phút.
mk3-w2.body:
CÂU HỎI: You are a new member of the Cooking Club. Tell us about the kind of food you like to cook.
SỐ TỪ: 20-30
BÀI MẪU: I like cooking simple Vietnamese dishes at home. I enjoy it because they are healthy and quick. For example, I often make fried rice with vegetables.

mk3-w3.title: Trả lời nhóm chat
mk3-w3.instr: Trả lời các thành viên trong nhóm chat, mỗi câu 30–40 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 10 phút.
mk3-w3.body:
NGƯỜI HỎI: Anna
CÂU HỎI: Hi! Welcome to the club. Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants? Why?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi Anna! I prefer eating at home rather than in restaurants. I like it because home-cooked food is cheaper and healthier. I also enjoy cooking with my family because it is a nice way to relax together.

NGƯỜI HỎI: Ben
CÂU HỎI: I want to learn to cook, but I don't have much time. Any advice?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi Ben! I suggest starting with simple dishes that take fifteen minutes. I recommend this because you will not feel stressed. For example, you could make an omelette or a stir-fry with vegetables after work.

NGƯỜI HỎI: Chloe
CÂU HỎI: Some people say young people don't know how to cook anymore. What do you think?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
