mk3-w4.intro: Email từ câu lạc bộ: "Dear member, The Cooking Club is planning to organise a food festival next month to raise money for a local children's hospital. Each member will be asked to cook one dish to sell. We are still deciding where to hold the festival and how to attract more visitors. We would like to hear your ideas."
mk3-w4.title: Viết 2 email
mk3-w4.instr: Email cho bạn khoảng 50 từ (thân mật) và email cho quản lý 120–150 từ (trang trọng). Khoảng 30 phút.
mk3-w4.body:
CÂU HỎI: Write an email to your friend, who is also a member of the club. Write about your feelings and what you plan to cook.
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi Lan,
I'm really excited about the club's food festival next month.
I think it's a great way to help the children's hospital.
I'm considering cooking spring rolls because they are easy to make and everyone loves them.
What do you think?
Talk soon,
Minh

CÂU HỎI: Write an email to the club manager. Write about your feelings and your ideas for the location and how to attract visitors.
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about the food festival planned for next month. I am very pleased that the club is raising money for the local children's hospital.
I would like to suggest holding the festival in the central park on a Sunday morning. I believe this location is ideal because many families go there at weekends and there is plenty of space for stalls. However, the weather might be a problem if it rains.
If the park is unavailable, we could use the hall at the community centre instead. I also suggest advertising the event on social media and in local schools, and offering a small prize for the best dish, so that more visitors will come.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Nguyen Minh

mk3-s1.title: Câu hỏi cá nhân
mk3-s1.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
mk3-s1.body:
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about your favourite season. | 30
BÀI MẪU: My favourite season is autumn. In my city, the weather is cool and dry, and the trees change colour, so it's lovely for walking. I also love autumn because there are many festivals, such as the Mid-Autumn Festival, when families get together and eat mooncakes.
CÂU HỎI: What do you usually do in the evening? | 30
BÀI MẪU: On weekday evenings, I usually have dinner with my family at about seven. After that, I spend an hour studying English, mostly listening and vocabulary. Before bed, I like to relax by reading or watching a short video, so that I can sleep well.
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a place you would like to visit. | 30
BÀI MẪU: I would really like to visit Japan, especially Kyoto. I've seen many photos of its old temples and gardens, and they look so peaceful. I'm also interested in Japanese food and culture, so I hope I can save enough money to go there in the next two years.

mk3-s2.part: Part 2 · Describe, express opinion, give reasons
mk3-s2.title: Mô tả ảnh
mk3-s2.instr: Mô tả bức ảnh rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Nội dung ảnh được mô tả bằng chữ.
mk3-s2.body:
ẢNH: Một quán cà phê đông người; vài người trẻ ngồi một mình làm việc trên máy tính xách tay, có cốc cà phê bên cạnh, ánh nắng chiếu qua cửa sổ lớn.
CÂU HỎI: Describe this picture. | 45
BÀI MẪU: This picture shows a busy coffee shop on what looks like a sunny day. In the foreground, there is a young woman sitting alone at a small table. She is working on her laptop and she seems very focused. Next to her, there is a cup of coffee. In the background, I can see several other people who are also using laptops or phones. The café has large windows, so it looks bright and comfortable. I think these people are probably students or freelancers who prefer working in a café rather than at home.
CÂU HỎI: Why do some people prefer working in cafés? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I think there are several reasons. First, working at home can be quite lonely and boring, while a café has a lively atmosphere, which helps some people feel more motivated. Second, there are fewer distractions than at home – for example, no housework or family members asking for help. Finally, cafés offer free Wi-Fi and coffee, so it's convenient. Personally, I sometimes study in a café at the weekend because it helps me concentrate.
CÂU HỎI: What are the disadvantages of working in public places? | 45
BÀI MẪU: The biggest disadvantage is noise. If the café is crowded, it can be hard to concentrate or join an online meeting. There's also a security problem, because people might see your screen or steal your laptop if you leave it for a moment. On top of that, it can be expensive, since you have to keep buying drinks. So in my opinion, cafés are good for short tasks, but not for important work.

mk3-s3.title: So sánh hai ảnh
mk3-s3.instr: Mô tả và so sánh hai bức ảnh, rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Nội dung ảnh được mô tả bằng chữ.
mk3-s3.body:
ẢNH: Ảnh 1: Một nhóm sinh viên đang học cùng nhau trong một thư viện lớn, yên tĩnh, có nhiều giá sách.
ẢNH: Ảnh 2: Một sinh viên đang học trực tuyến một mình tại nhà, đeo tai nghe, nhìn vào màn hình máy tính.
CÂU HỎI: Tell me what you see in the two pictures. | 45
BÀI MẪU: Both pictures show people studying, but in very different ways. In the first picture, there is a group of students in a large library. They are sitting around a table with books and notes, and they seem to be helping each other. The atmosphere looks quiet and serious. In contrast, the second picture shows a young man studying alone at home. He's wearing headphones and looking at a computer screen, so I guess he's attending an online class. While the first picture shows teamwork, the second shows independent learning.
CÂU HỎI: Which way of studying is better, in your opinion? Why? | 45
BÀI MẪU: In my opinion, studying in a library with other people is more effective, at least for me. When I study with classmates, we can explain difficult points to each other, and I feel more motivated because everyone is working hard. At home, I easily get distracted by my phone or the TV. However, online learning is more flexible and saves travelling time, so it suits people who have a job or live far from school.
CÂU HỎI: Do you think online learning will replace traditional classrooms? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I don't think online learning will completely replace classrooms. It's true that it has become very popular, especially since the pandemic, and it's great for adults who are busy. But young students need face-to-face contact to develop social skills, and teachers can notice problems more easily in a real classroom. I believe the future will be a mixture of both, where some lessons are online and others are in person.

mk3-s4.title: Learning a new skill
mk3-s4.instr: Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu.
mk3-s4.body:
ẢNH: Một người lớn tuổi đang học chơi đàn guitar với sự hướng dẫn của một người trẻ.
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a time when you learned a new skill.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about the time I learned to swim. It happened when I was in my first year at university. I had always been afraid of water, but my friends often went to the beach, and I felt embarrassed that I couldn't join them. So I signed up for a course at a local swimming pool. For the first few lessons, I was really nervous, but the teacher was very patient.
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel about it?
BÀI MẪU: At first, I felt frustrated because other learners improved faster than me. However, after about a month, I could swim twenty-five metres without stopping, and I felt extremely proud of myself. It also taught me that being afraid is normal, and that practice can help us overcome our fears.
CÂU HỎI: Is it more difficult for adults to learn new skills than children? Why?
BÀI MẪU: In my opinion, it is generally more difficult for adults. Children have more free time and they aren't afraid of making mistakes, so they learn quickly. Adults, on the other hand, are busy with work and family, and they often worry about looking silly. That said, adults usually have stronger motivation and better discipline, so if they really want to learn something, they can be just as successful.

Recycling at home is easier than many people think.
To begin with, find out which materials your local council collects.
Then put separate bins for paper, plastic and glass in your kitchen.

This stops the bins from smelling and makes the materials easier to process.
Once it becomes a habit, recycling takes almost no extra time.

mk4-r3.intro:
Helen: As a mother of two teenagers, I've seen how social media affects their mood. My daughter compares herself to influencers all the time and often feels she isn't good enough. I don't want to ban it, but we have a rule: no phones at the dinner table or after ten o'clock.

Kevin: I'm a secondary school teacher, and I think adults worry too much. Teenagers use social media to share ideas, learn new skills and even organise charity events. The real problem isn't the apps themselves – it's that schools don't teach young people how to use them sensibly.

Thu: I'm nineteen, and I deleted most of my accounts last year. I was spending four or five hours a day scrolling, and my exam results suffered. Now I only use a messaging app to stay in touch with friends, and I feel much calmer.

mk4-r4.title: Ghép tiêu đề: rác thải nhựa trong đại dương
mk4-r4.instr: Bài đọc dài khoảng 750 từ như đề thật. Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Có 8 tiêu đề cho 7 đoạn, một tiêu đề thừa.
mk4-r4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: A material that changed the world | Hope from new materials | Invisible pieces, visible problems | Plastic is not the real problem | Small actions, big difference | The journey from land to sea | Who should pay? | Wildlife in danger
When plastic was first produced on a large scale in the 1950s, it seemed like a miracle. It was cheap, light, strong and could be shaped into almost anything, from toys and bottles to car parts and medical equipment. Within a few decades, it had replaced glass, metal and paper in thousands of everyday products. Global production has grown from around two million tonnes a year in 1950 to more than four hundred million tonnes today. The qualities that made plastic so useful, however, are exactly the ones that now make it such a serious environmental problem. Because it is designed to last, a single plastic bottle can remain in the environment for hundreds of years. = A material that changed the world
Scientists estimate that between eight and twelve million tonnes of plastic enter the oceans every year. Surprisingly, only a small part of it is thrown directly into the sea by ships or fishermen. Most begins its journey on land. Rubbish dropped in streets is washed into drains by rain, carried into rivers and eventually reaches the coast. In countries without good waste collection systems, large amounts of rubbish are left in open dumps near rivers, where it is easily blown or washed away. Ten major rivers, mostly in Asia and Africa, are believed to carry a large share of all the plastic that reaches the ocean. = The journey from land to sea
The effects on marine animals are well documented and often shocking. Sea turtles mistake plastic bags for jellyfish, one of their main foods, and seabirds feed pieces of plastic to their chicks. When animals swallow plastic, their stomachs can become full of material they cannot digest, and they slowly starve. Others become trapped in old fishing nets, which continue to catch fish and dolphins for years after they have been lost. Researchers have found plastic in the stomachs of whales washed up on beaches around the world, sometimes weighing more than twenty kilograms. Conservation groups warn that, without urgent action, several endangered species could be pushed even closer to extinction. = Wildlife in danger
In recent years, attention has turned to an even smaller threat. Over time, sunlight and waves break plastic into tiny fragments known as microplastics, many of them smaller than a grain of rice. Microplastics are also released when we wash clothes made from synthetic materials such as polyester. These particles have now been found everywhere, from the deepest ocean trenches to Arctic ice, and even in drinking water and salt. Scientists do not yet fully understand how they affect human health, but many are worried, since fish and shellfish that we eat regularly are known to contain them. Some studies have even detected tiny particles in human blood, although researchers stress that much more work is needed before firm conclusions can be drawn. = Invisible pieces, visible problems
There is a fierce debate about who is responsible for solving the problem. Some argue that consumers must change their behaviour, while others insist that companies which produce plastic packaging should be made to pay for collecting and recycling it. Several countries have introduced laws of this kind, often called "producer responsibility" schemes. Supporters say they encourage companies to use less packaging. Critics, however, claim that the extra costs are simply passed on to shoppers through higher prices. Many economists believe that a combination of both approaches, together with clear labelling on packaging, offers the best chance of real progress. = Who should pay?
Meanwhile, scientists and engineers are developing alternatives. Packaging made from seaweed, mushrooms and even milk proteins is being tested, and some of these materials break down naturally within weeks. Researchers have also discovered bacteria that can digest certain types of plastic, which could one day help to clean up waste that already exists. These solutions are promising, but most are still expensive and not yet available on a large scale. Experts warn that they should not become an excuse to keep producing huge amounts of plastic in the meantime. Governments could speed up progress by funding research and by offering tax benefits to companies that switch to these new materials. = Hope from new materials
Individuals can also make a real contribution. Carrying a reusable bag and water bottle, refusing plastic straws and choosing products with less packaging may seem minor, but when millions of people do the same, the effect is significant. In Ireland, for example, a small charge on plastic bags reduced their use by more than ninety percent in just a few months. Beach clean-ups organised by volunteers remove tonnes of rubbish every year and, perhaps more importantly, raise awareness. Most experts agree that no single solution will be enough, but that everyday choices still matter. = Small actions, big difference

mk4-lp1.title: Nghe và chọn chi tiết
mk4-lp1.instr: Nghe từng đoạn và chọn đáp án đúng. Mỗi đoạn được nghe tối đa 2 lần.
mk4-lp1.body:
Listen to a message from a dentist. When is the new appointment?
W: Hello, this is Bright Smile Dental Clinic calling for Mr Patel. I'm afraid Doctor Green is ill on Tuesday, so we need to move your appointment. We can offer you Thursday at two fifteen. Please call us to confirm.
*Thursday at 2:15
Tuesday at 2:15
Thursday at 2:50
? "We can offer you Thursday at two fifteen."

A woman is talking about her new flat. What does she like most?
W: The flat is quite small and the kitchen is a bit old-fashioned. But the view from the balcony is incredible – I can see the whole river. I sit out there every evening.
*The view
The kitchen
The size
? "the view from the balcony is incredible".

Listen to a man at a train station. Where is he going?
M: Hi, one return ticket to Manchester, please. Oh, sorry, I mean Liverpool. I'm changing trains in Manchester, but I'm going to Liverpool.
*Liverpool
Manchester
London
? Đổi tàu ở Manchester, điểm đến là Liverpool.

Listen to two friends. What will they buy for Tom's birthday?
W: How about a book for Tom? He loves reading.
M: He's got hundreds already. What about a watch?
W: Too expensive. Let's get him concert tickets – his favourite band is playing next month.
M: Perfect.
*Concert tickets
A book
A watch

Listen to an announcement at a supermarket. What is on special offer?
M: Good morning, shoppers. Today only, all fresh fruit is half price. Don't miss our bakery, where bread is freshly baked every hour.

Bread
Vegetables

Listen to a woman talking about her journey to work. How long does it take?
W: When I lived in the city centre, it took me ten minutes to walk to work. Now I live in the suburbs, so I drive, and with all the traffic it takes forty minutes.

10 minutes
14 minutes

Listen to a man phoning a hotel. What is the problem?
M: Hello, I'm in room 305. The heating is working fine now, thanks, but there's no hot water in the shower. Could someone come and look at it?
*There is no hot water
The heating is broken
The room is noisy

Listen to a tour guide. What will the group do first?
W: Welcome, everyone. Before we visit the castle, we're going to have lunch at a traditional restaurant in the village. After that, we'll take a boat trip on the lake.
*Have lunch
Visit the castle
Take a boat trip
? "Before we visit the castle, we're going to have lunch".

Listen to a student talking about her course. Which subject does she find hardest?
W: I'm enjoying my business course. Marketing is fun and I'm good at economics. But accounting – all those numbers – I really struggle with that.
*Accounting
Marketing
Economics
? "accounting… I really struggle with that".

Listen to two colleagues. What does the woman want the man to do?
W: Mark, could you print the reports for the meeting? I've already booked the room and sent the invitations.
M: Sure, no problem.
*Print some reports
Book a room
Send invitations
? Cô đã đặt phòng và gửi lời mời.

Listen to a radio report. Why is the road closed?
M: The main road into town is closed this morning. Earlier reports suggested an accident, but in fact a tree fell across the road during last night's storm. Workers expect to clear it by midday.
*A tree fell on it
There was an accident
Workers are repairing it
? "a tree fell across the road".

Listen to a man talking about his weekend. What did he do on Saturday?
M: I'd planned to go hiking on Saturday, but it rained all day, so I stayed home and cleaned the house. Luckily, Sunday was sunny, and I finally went climbing in the hills.
*He cleaned the house
He went hiking
He went climbing
? Thứ Bảy mưa → ở nhà dọn dẹp.

Listen to a woman ordering food. What does she order to drink?
W: I'll have the chicken salad, please. And to drink… not coffee at this time of day. Orange juice? No, actually, just a sparkling water, please.
*Sparkling water
Coffee
Orange juice
? Cuối cùng chọn sparkling water.

mk4-lp2.title: Ghép người nói
mk4-lp2.instr: Four people are talking about their hobbies. Match each speaker with what they say about their hobby. There are two extra options.
mk4-lp2.body:
LỰA CHỌN: It costs a lot of money | It has helped my career | It helps me meet people | It keeps me healthy | It makes me feel calm | It takes up too much time
Speaker A = It makes me feel calm
M: I started painting about three years ago when I was very stressed at work. When I'm in front of the canvas, I forget about everything else. My mind becomes quiet, and after an hour I feel completely relaxed.
Speaker B = It helps me meet people
W: I joined a choir after I moved to a new city where I didn't know anybody. Now I've got a wonderful group of friends. We rehearse on Wednesdays, but we often go for dinner afterwards and meet up at weekends too.
Speaker C = It has helped my career
M: I've been making short films as a hobby since I was a teenager. Last year, one of my films won a small competition, and an advertising agency saw it and offered me a job. I never expected a hobby to lead to work.
Speaker D = It costs a lot of money
W: I love photography, but it's an expensive hobby. A good camera body is only the beginning – then you need lenses, a tripod, editing software… I've spent far more than I planned, and I'm still not satisfied with my equipment.

mk4-lp3.audio:
W: Are you going abroad again this summer?
M: No, I want to explore my own country this year. Flying is getting so expensive.
W: That's true, prices have gone up a lot. But I still think travelling abroad teaches you more – new languages, new cultures.
M: You can learn a lot at home too. There are so many places here I've never seen.
W: Maybe. For me, the problem with local holidays is the weather. You can't rely on it.
M: I don't mind a bit of rain. And it's better for the environment not to fly.
W: Well, I agree with you there. I feel guilty about flying so often.
mk4-lp3.title: Ai có ý kiến này?
mk4-lp3.instr: A man and a woman are discussing holidays. Decide whose opinion matches each statement: the man, the woman, or both.
mk4-lp3.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Man | Woman | Both
Flights have become more expensive. = Both
Travelling abroad is more educational. = Woman
The weather makes local holidays risky. = Woman
Flying is bad for the environment. = Both

mk4-lp4a.audio: M: Electric cars are often presented as the answer to pollution in our cities, and it's true that they produce no exhaust fumes. But we need to be careful. Building the batteries uses a lot of energy and rare metals, and if the electricity comes from coal power stations, the overall benefit is much smaller than people think. I'm not against electric cars – I drive one myself. My point is that replacing every petrol car with an electric one won't solve traffic jams or the lack of space in cities. The real priority should be making public transport, cycling and walking more attractive, so that fewer people need a car at all.
mk4-lp4a.title: Bài nói 1
mk4-lp4a.instr: Listen to a transport expert talking about electric cars. Answer two questions.
mk4-lp4a.body:
What is the speaker's attitude towards electric cars?
*They have benefits but also limitations
They are completely useless
They will solve pollution problems
? "I'm not against electric cars… My point is that replacing every petrol car… won't solve traffic jams".

What does the speaker think should be the main priority?
*Reducing the need for cars
Building more charging stations
Producing cheaper batteries
? "The real priority should be making public transport, cycling and walking more attractive".

mk4-lp4b.audio: W: People imagine that writers wait for inspiration and then write all night. For me, it's the opposite. I write every morning from seven until eleven, whether I feel inspired or not. Some days, I produce five pages; on bad days, just a paragraph. But the habit is what matters. The afternoons I keep for reading, walking and answering emails. When I was younger, I tried writing only when I felt like it, and I never finished anything. Discipline, not talent, is what turned me from someone who wanted to write into a writer.
mk4-lp4b.title: Bài nói 2
mk4-lp4b.instr: Listen to a novelist talking about her writing routine. Answer two questions.
mk4-lp4b.body:
How does the writer describe her approach to work?
*She follows a fixed daily routine
She writes only when she feels inspired
She works mostly at night
? "I write every morning from seven until eleven, whether I feel inspired or not."

What does she believe made her successful?
*Being disciplined
Having natural talent
Reading a lot
? "Discipline, not talent, is what turned me… into a writer."

mk4-w1.title: Trả lời tin nhắn ngắn
mk4-w1.instr: Trả lời mỗi tin nhắn bằng 1–5 từ. Nên xong trong khoảng 3 phút.
mk4-w1.body:
CÂU HỎI: Do you have a garden?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Yes, a small one.

CÂU HỎI: What's your favourite flower?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Roses, especially red ones.

CÂU HỎI: How often do you water your plants?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Every morning.

CÂU HỎI: What's the weather like today?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: Sunny and quite hot.

CÂU HỎI: What do you do at weekends?
SỐ TỪ: 1-5
BÀI MẪU: I visit my grandparents.

mk4-w2.title: Viết đoạn ngắn
mk4-w2.instr: Trả lời bằng câu hoàn chỉnh, 20–30 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 7 phút.
mk4-w2.body:
CÂU HỎI: You are a new member of the Gardening Club. Tell us why you are interested in gardening.
SỐ TỪ: 20-30
BÀI MẪU: I am interested in gardening because it helps me relax. I like it because I can grow my own food. For example, I grow herbs on my balcony.

mk4-w3.title: Trả lời nhóm chat
mk4-w3.instr: Trả lời các thành viên trong nhóm chat, mỗi câu 30–40 từ. Nên làm trong khoảng 10 phút.
mk4-w3.body:
NGƯỜI HỎI: Peter
CÂU HỎI: Hi! What is the best way for a beginner to start gardening?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi Peter! I suggest starting with a few easy plants in pots. I recommend this because they need little space and care. For example, mint and basil grow quickly and you can use them for cooking.

NGƯỜI HỎI: Mia
CÂU HỎI: Do you prefer growing flowers or vegetables? Why?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi Mia! I prefer growing vegetables rather than flowers. I like it because I can eat fresh, healthy food from my own garden. I also save money because I buy fewer vegetables at the market.

NGƯỜI HỎI: Sam
CÂU HỎI: Should cities create more green spaces? What do you think?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi Sam! Yes, I strongly agree that cities need more green spaces. I think so because trees reduce air pollution and heat. I also believe parks give people a place to relax and exercise after work.

mk4-w4.intro: Email từ câu lạc bộ: "Dear member, The Gardening Club has been offered a piece of empty land behind the local school. We are planning to turn it into a community garden, but we need to decide what to grow there and how to get local people involved. Please send us your ideas."
mk4-w4.title: Viết 2 email
mk4-w4.instr: Email cho bạn khoảng 50 từ (thân mật) và email cho quản lý 120–150 từ (trang trọng). Khoảng 30 phút.
mk4-w4.body:
CÂU HỎI: Write an email to your friend, who is also a member of the club. Write about your feelings and what you would like to grow.
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi Nam,
I'm really excited about the club's plan for a community garden.
I think it will make the area behind the school much more beautiful.
I'm considering suggesting fruit trees because children would love picking fruit.
What do you think?
Best wishes,
Linh

CÂU HỎI: Write an email to the club president. Write about your feelings and your ideas for the garden and how to involve local people.
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about the plan to create a community garden behind the local school. I am very pleased that the club has been offered this land.
I would like to suggest growing vegetables and herbs, together with a small area of flowers. I believe this would be both useful and attractive, and the vegetables could be given to families in need. However, the garden will need regular care, especially during the hot summer months.
If it is not possible to find enough volunteers, we could ask students from the school to help as part of their science lessons. I also suggest organising a planting day at the weekend and inviting local residents, so that everyone feels the garden belongs to them.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Tran Linh

mk4-s1.title: Câu hỏi cá nhân
mk4-s1.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
mk4-s1.body:
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about your hometown. | 30
BÀI MẪU: I come from Hai Phong, a port city in the north of Vietnam. It's famous for its seafood and its red flame trees, which bloom in summer. The city is not as crowded as Hanoi, so life is quite relaxed, and people there are very friendly and direct.
CÂU HỎI: What kind of music do you like? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I mostly listen to pop and acoustic music. I like songs with meaningful lyrics, and I often listen to them while I'm commuting or doing housework. Recently, I've also started listening to English songs, because they help me improve my pronunciation and learn new expressions.
CÂU HỎI: How do you usually spend your holidays? | 30
BÀI MẪU: During long holidays, I usually go back to my hometown to visit my parents. If I have enough time, I travel with my friends to the beach or the mountains. I prefer short trips with a relaxed schedule, because I want to rest rather than rush from place to place.

mk4-s2.part: Part 2 · Describe, express opinion, give reasons
mk4-s2.title: Mô tả ảnh
mk4-s2.instr: Mô tả bức ảnh rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Nội dung ảnh được mô tả bằng chữ.
mk4-s2.body:
ẢNH: Một gia đình gồm bố mẹ và hai con nhỏ đang ăn dã ngoại trên bãi cỏ trong công viên; có một tấm thảm, giỏ thức ăn và một con chó.
CÂU HỎI: Describe this picture. | 45
BÀI MẪU: In this picture, I can see a family having a picnic in a park on a sunny day. The parents are sitting on a blanket on the grass, and there's a basket full of food and drinks next to them. Their two young children are playing with a dog nearby, and everyone looks very happy and relaxed. In the background, there are tall green trees, so I think it's probably spring or summer. It seems like a perfect weekend for a family.
CÂU HỎI: Why is it important for families to spend time outdoors? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I think spending time outdoors is important for both health and relationships. Children get exercise and fresh air instead of sitting in front of screens all day. Parents can also relax and forget about work for a while. Most importantly, outdoor activities like picnics or walks give families a chance to talk and have fun together, which helps them build stronger bonds.
CÂU HỎI: What do families in your country usually do at weekends? | 45
BÀI MẪU: In Vietnam, many families visit their grandparents or relatives at weekends and have a big meal together. In the cities, families often go to shopping malls, because they're air-conditioned and have restaurants and play areas for children. Some families go to the park in the early morning to exercise. However, because parents are busy, some children spend most of the weekend studying at extra classes.

mk4-s3.title: So sánh hai ảnh
mk4-s3.instr: Mô tả và so sánh hai bức ảnh, rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Nội dung ảnh được mô tả bằng chữ.
mk4-s3.body:
ẢNH: Ảnh 1: Một khu chợ truyền thống đông đúc, người bán rau quả ngồi bên các sạp hàng, người mua đang mặc cả.
ẢNH: Ảnh 2: Một siêu thị hiện đại, sạch sẽ, có nhiều kệ hàng và một người đang đẩy xe mua sắm.
CÂU HỎI: Tell me what you see in the two pictures. | 45
BÀI MẪU: Both pictures show places where people buy food. The first one is a traditional market. It's very crowded and lively, with sellers sitting next to piles of fresh fruit and vegetables, and customers seem to be bargaining with them. The second picture shows a modern supermarket, which looks much cleaner and more organised. There are long shelves full of products, and a woman is pushing a trolley calmly down an aisle. So the first place feels busy and noisy, while the second feels quiet and comfortable.
CÂU HỎI: Where do you prefer to go shopping? Why? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I usually prefer the supermarket, mainly because it's convenient. I can buy everything in one place, prices are clearly marked, and I can pay by card. It's also air-conditioned, which is nice in summer. However, for fresh vegetables and fish, my mother always goes to the local market, because the food is fresher and often cheaper, and she knows the sellers personally.
CÂU HỎI: Do you think traditional markets will disappear in the future? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I don't think they will disappear completely, but they may become smaller. Young people are increasingly shopping in supermarkets or online, because they're busy and want convenience. On the other hand, markets are an important part of our culture, and many tourists love visiting them. If local governments improve hygiene and facilities in markets, I believe they can continue to exist alongside modern shops.

mk4-s4.title: An important decision
mk4-s4.instr: Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu.
mk4-s4.body:
ẢNH: Một người trẻ đứng trước ngã ba đường, nhìn hai hướng khác nhau.
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about an important decision you have made.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about the decision to choose my university major. When I finished high school, my parents wanted me to study medicine, because they believed it was a safe and respected career. However, I was much more interested in business and languages. After thinking about it for weeks and talking to my teachers, I decided to study international business.
CÂU HỎI: How did you feel after making the decision?
BÀI MẪU: At first, I felt quite nervous and a little guilty, because I didn't want to disappoint my parents. But once I started the course, I realised it was the right choice. I enjoyed my classes and got good results, and eventually my parents became proud of me.
CÂU HỎI: Should young people make their own decisions about their future? Why or why not?
BÀI MẪU: In my opinion, young people should make the final decision themselves, because they are the ones who will live with the result. If they follow a path they're not interested in, they may feel unhappy for many years. That said, they should listen to advice from parents and teachers, who have more life experience. So the best approach is to make decisions independently but not alone.

mk5-core-g.title: Ngữ pháp: 25 câu

I ___ to Paris three times, but I've never seen the Eiffel Tower at night.

went
was

do

miss

to smoke
smoke

took
have taken

studied

buy

a

mk5-core-v1.title: Từ vựng: từ đồng nghĩa
mk5-core-v1.instr: Chọn từ có nghĩa gần nhất với từ bên trái. 10 lựa chọn, 5 lựa chọn không dùng đến.
mk5-core-v1.body:

mk5-core-v2.instr: Chọn từ phù hợp với từng định nghĩa.
mk5-core-v2.body:

a shop where you can buy medicine = pharmacy

a place where boats are kept safely = harbour

mk5-core-v3.title: Từ vựng: hoàn thành câu

mk5-core-v3.body:

mk5-core-v4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: a bath | a conclusion | a party | a question | a risk | an accident | birth | business | permission | someone a lift
throw = a party
ask for = permission
come to = a conclusion
give = someone a lift
take = a risk

mk5-core-v5.title: Từ vựng: ghép định nghĩa (nâng cao)
mk5-core-v5.instr: Chọn từ phù hợp với từng định nghĩa.
mk5-core-v5.body:
LỰA CHỌN: brochure | budget | census | headline | interval | itinerary | outcome | proposal | shortage | survey
a plan of a journey, including places to visit = itinerary
the amount of money available to spend = budget

mk5-r2a.body:
Saving money every month can seem impossible when prices keep rising.
However, the first step is simply to know where your money goes.
For one month, write down everything you spend, even small things like coffee.
At the end of the month, you will probably be surprised by the total.
Then choose two or three areas where you can easily spend less.
Put the money you save into a separate account so you are not tempted to use it.

After lunch, I was allowed to take two of the dogs for a walk.
One of them, a shy brown dog called Biscuit, followed me everywhere afterwards.
By the end of the day, I had decided to come back every weekend.

mk5-r4.title: Ghép tiêu đề: vì sao chúng ta trì hoãn
mk5-r4.instr: Bài đọc dài khoảng 750 từ như đề thật. Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Có 8 tiêu đề cho 7 đoạn, một tiêu đề thừa.
mk5-r4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: A habit almost everyone shares | Breaking tasks into pieces | Feelings, not laziness | Perfectionists at risk | The cost of waiting | The present self versus the future self | Technology makes it worse | Why deadlines always work
Almost everyone has done it. You have an important report to write, but instead you check your messages, tidy your desk or suddenly decide that the kitchen needs cleaning. Procrastination, the habit of delaying tasks we know we should do, is one of the most common human behaviours. Surveys suggest that around twenty percent of adults are regular procrastinators, and among university students the figure may be as high as eighty percent. For a long time, it was seen simply as a sign of poor time management or a weak character. Recent research, however, paints a more complicated picture, and it suggests that the usual advice to "just get on with it" rarely helps. = A habit almost everyone shares
Psychologists now believe that procrastination has more to do with emotions than with laziness. When a task makes us feel anxious, bored or uncertain, we look for something that will make us feel better immediately. Watching a video or chatting with a friend provides that relief, so we choose it instead. The problem is that the relief is temporary. The task is still there, and now we also feel guilty about avoiding it, which makes it even less attractive. In this way, procrastination becomes a cycle that is difficult to break. People who procrastinate are often not lazy at all; they may work extremely hard on other things. Understanding this emotional side is important, because it means that simply telling people to try harder is unlikely to change their behaviour. = Feelings, not laziness
Another explanation involves the way our brains think about time. Studies using brain scans have found that when people think about themselves in the distant future, their brain activity looks similar to when they think about a stranger. In other words, we tend to treat our "future self" as a different person. So when we put off a difficult task, we are, in a sense, passing the problem on to someone else. This also explains why it is so easy to promise that we will start exercising or saving money "next month", but so hard to begin today. Some researchers have found that showing people realistic images of their older selves makes them more willing to save money for the future. = The present self versus the future self
Interestingly, people who want everything to be perfect are especially likely to procrastinate. If you believe that your work must be excellent, starting it can feel frightening, because there is a risk that the result will not meet your high standards. By delaying, perfectionists can tell themselves that they could have done better if they had had more time. This protects their self-image, but it often leads to rushed, lower-quality work, which in turn makes them more anxious about the next task. Coaches who work with perfectionists often encourage them to aim for work that is "good enough" rather than flawless, at least for a first attempt. = Perfectionists at risk
The effects of chronic procrastination can be serious. Students who regularly delay their work tend to get lower grades and report higher levels of stress. In the workplace, missed deadlines can damage careers and relationships with colleagues. There are health costs too: people who put off tasks are also more likely to delay visiting a doctor or making healthy changes to their lifestyle. Researchers have even linked long-term procrastination to poor sleep, as people stay up late trying to finish work they could have completed earlier. Over many years, the combination of stress and missed opportunities can have a significant effect on a person's overall satisfaction with life. = The cost of waiting
Modern life has made the problem harder to escape. Our phones and computers offer an endless supply of instant entertainment, and apps are designed to capture our attention. A quick look at social media can easily turn into an hour. Many people now work on the same device that provides these distractions, so the temptation is always only one click away. Some experts recommend turning off notifications or using apps that block certain websites during working hours. Others suggest keeping the phone in a different room altogether, since even having it on the desk has been shown to reduce concentration. = Technology makes it worse
So what actually helps? One of the most effective strategies is to break large tasks into very small steps. Instead of planning to "write the report", you might decide to "write the first paragraph" or simply "open the document". Small steps feel less threatening, and once people start, they often find it easier to continue. Being kind to yourself also matters. Studies have shown that students who forgave themselves for procrastinating on one exam were less likely to procrastinate before the next. Setting a fixed time to start, rather than waiting until you feel ready, can also make a surprising difference to how much gets done. = Breaking tasks into pieces

mk5-lp4a.audio: W: When people hear the phrase "green building", they often imagine solar panels on the roof. Solar panels are useful, but in my experience, the most important decisions are much simpler. Which way does the building face? How big are the windows? Is it well insulated? Get these things right, and a building needs very little energy for heating or cooling. Unfortunately, many developers still focus on the cost of construction rather than the cost of running a building over fifty years. A cheaper building often turns out to be far more expensive in the long run. Until clients start thinking long term, progress will remain slow.

mk5-lp4b.audio: M: In my first restaurant, we threw away nearly a third of the food we bought. It was shocking, but nobody talked about it – that was just how the industry worked. What changed my mind was looking at the numbers. Food waste was costing us more than our electricity bill. So we made small changes: smaller portions with free refills of rice and bread, a daily menu based on what needed to be used up, and staff meals made from leftovers. Waste fell by seventy percent. Honestly, I wish I'd done it years earlier. It wasn't only good for the planet; it saved the business.

mk5-s2.part: Part 2 · Describe, express opinion, give reasons
mk5-s2.title: Mô tả ảnh
mk5-s2.instr: Mô tả bức ảnh rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Nội dung ảnh được mô tả bằng chữ.
mk5-s2.body:
ẢNH: Một nhóm tình nguyện viên trẻ mặc áo phông giống nhau, đeo găng tay, đang nhặt rác trên bãi biển và cho vào túi lớn.
CÂU HỎI: Describe this picture. | 45
BÀI MẪU: This picture shows a group of young volunteers cleaning a beach. They are wearing matching T-shirts, so I think they belong to the same organisation or school. Most of them are wearing gloves and holding large bags, and they're picking up rubbish such as plastic bottles from the sand. In the background, I can see the sea and a clear blue sky. Although the work looks tiring, everyone seems cheerful and proud of what they're doing.
CÂU HỎI: Why do people do volunteer work? | 45
BÀI MẪU: People volunteer for many different reasons. Many of them simply want to help their community or protect the environment. Others, especially young people, volunteer to gain experience and skills such as teamwork and communication, which look good on a CV. Volunteering is also a great way to meet like-minded people. Personally, I think the feeling of doing something meaningful is the main reason.
CÂU HỎI: Should schools require students to do volunteer work? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I think it's a good idea for schools to encourage volunteering, but I'm not sure it should be compulsory. If students are forced to volunteer, some of them may do it without any real interest. However, a short required programme could help students discover causes they care about. So maybe schools should offer a variety of projects and let students choose which one to join.

Through the window, I can see tall buildings, so it's probably on a high floor. It looks stylish but quite compact. The second picture shows a large house in the countryside, with a big garden and green fields all around. It looks peaceful and spacious, but it seems far from shops and other services.

There are also more restaurants, cinemas and hospitals nearby. However, when I'm older and have children, I might choose the countryside house, because children need space and fresh air to play.

BÀI MẪU: The main reason is jobs. Most companies and factories are located in or near big cities, so young people move there to find work with better salaries. Cities also offer better education and healthcare. In addition, many young people are attracted by the lively lifestyle and entertainment. Unfortunately, this causes problems such as traffic jams, pollution and high housing prices.

CÂU HỎI: How did it make you feel?
BÀI MẪU: I felt really happy and proud. They thanked me many times and even invited me for a coffee. It was also a good chance for me to practise my English in a real situation, and it made me realise that small acts of kindness can make a big difference to someone's day.
CÂU HỎI: Are people less willing to help strangers nowadays? Why?
BÀI MẪU: In some ways, I think they are. In big cities, people are always busy and they often look at their phones instead of noticing what's happening around them. Some people are also afraid of being cheated. However, I don't think people are less kind. When there's a natural disaster, for example, many people donate money or volunteer. So I would say people still want to help, but daily life makes it harder.

mk6-r2a.title: Sắp xếp câu: chuẩn bị cho chuyến bay dài
mk6-r2a.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại thành đoạn văn hợp lý.
mk6-r2a.body:
A long-haul flight can be exhausting, but a little planning helps a lot.
A few days before you travel, try to adjust your sleep to the time zone of your destination.
On the day of the flight, wear loose, comfortable clothes and pack a light jumper.
Once you are on the plane, drink plenty of water and avoid too much coffee.
It is also a good idea to walk up and down the aisle every couple of hours.
Doing this will improve your circulation and help you feel less stiff when you land.

mk6-r2b.title: Sắp xếp câu: chuyến bay suýt lỡ
mk6-r2b.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại thành đoạn văn hợp lý.
mk6-r2b.body:
Last year, I almost missed a flight to Singapore.
I had set my alarm for five o'clock, but I forgot to switch it on.
As a result, I woke up just one hour before the plane was due to leave.
I grabbed my bag and took a taxi, begging the driver to go as fast as possible.
When I finally reached the check-in desk, it was just about to close.
Since then, I always set two alarms the night before I travel.

Grace: My neighbour's dog barks for hours every day while she's at work. I love animals, but it's unfair on everyone else in the building. If a building allows pets, there need to be clear rules, and owners who break them should be fined.

Tuan: I'd love a dog, but my apartment is tiny and I work long hours. It wouldn't be fair on the animal. Maybe when I have a house with a garden, I'll get one. Until then, I volunteer at a shelter at weekends.

Olivia: Research shows that pets reduce stress and loneliness, especially for older people who live alone. My grandmother's small dog is her best companion. Banning pets in apartments would hurt the people who need them most.

mk6-r4.title: Ghép tiêu đề: học ngoại ngữ khi trưởng thành
mk6-r4.instr: Bài đọc dài khoảng 750 từ như đề thật. Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Có 8 tiêu đề cho 7 đoạn, một tiêu đề thừa.
mk6-r4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Advantages of an adult brain | Is it ever too late? | Learning through real use | Making time in a busy life | Mistakes are part of the process | The accent question | The myth of the "language gene" | Why children seem to learn faster
Many adults who want to learn a new language give up before they even begin. They have heard that languages are best learned in childhood, and they assume that after a certain age it is simply too late. This belief is widespread, but it is only partly true. While it is generally accepted that young children have certain advantages, studies show that adults can reach a high level in a foreign language, and some even become as fluent as native speakers. The real question is not whether adults can learn, but how they learn most effectively. Many successful language learners did not start until their thirties, forties or even later, often because of a new job, a partner or a move abroad. = Is it ever too late?
It is easy to understand why children appear to pick up languages so effortlessly. A child who moves to a new country is surrounded by the language all day, at school, in the playground and on television. Children are also less afraid of sounding silly, so they speak freely and receive constant feedback. They have years to absorb the language before anyone expects them to discuss complex topics. Adults, in contrast, usually study for a few hours a week in a classroom and are expected to make rapid progress. When the conditions are so different, the comparison is hardly fair. Seen in this light, the supposed advantage of children has as much to do with their circumstances as with their age. = Why children seem to learn faster
In fact, adults have several important advantages. They already understand how language works, so they can learn grammar rules consciously and apply them. They have a much larger vocabulary in their first language, which helps them guess the meaning of related words. Adults are also better at using learning strategies, such as making flashcards, setting goals and finding useful resources online. In controlled studies, adult beginners often make faster progress than children in the first months of learning, especially in reading and grammar. They are also usually able to organise their own learning, choosing materials that match their interests and their professional needs. = Advantages of an adult brain
The area where age seems to matter most is pronunciation. People who start learning after their early teens rarely lose their accent completely. However, many linguists argue that this is not a serious problem. The purpose of learning a language, for most people, is to communicate clearly, not to be mistaken for a native speaker. Millions of people use English successfully every day with a strong accent. What matters is that the listener can understand, and clear pronunciation can certainly be developed at any age with practice. In international settings, in fact, speakers with a clear but non-native accent are sometimes easier to understand than native speakers who talk very quickly. = The accent question
Another common belief is that some people are simply born with a talent for languages. It is true that people differ in their memory and their sensitivity to sounds, but research suggests that motivation and practice are far more important than any natural ability. Learners who believe they are "bad at languages" often stop trying when they find something difficult, while those who believe they can improve keep going. In the end, the second group usually succeeds, regardless of how talented they seemed at the start. Teachers therefore try to build learners' confidence early, by setting achievable goals and pointing out the progress they have already made. = The myth of the "language gene"
For adults with jobs and families, the biggest challenge is often finding time. Experts recommend short, regular sessions rather than long, occasional ones. Fifteen minutes a day with a language app, a podcast during the commute or a few pages of a graded reader before bed can add up to hundreds of hours over a year. Linking study to existing routines, such as listening to the news in the target language while making breakfast, makes it more likely that the habit will continue. Many learners also find it helpful to join an online group or find a study partner, because promising to meet someone makes it harder to skip a session. = Making time in a busy life
Finally, adults need to accept that making mistakes is unavoidable. Many adult learners feel embarrassed when they make errors, so they avoid speaking until they feel "ready", a moment which may never come. Teachers say that the learners who progress fastest are usually those who are willing to speak imperfectly and learn from the corrections they receive. Every mistake is evidence that the learner is trying something new. As one teacher put it, the only learners who never make mistakes are the ones who never open their mouths. Learners who accept this idea usually enjoy the process more, and enjoyment is one of the strongest predictors of long-term success. = Mistakes are part of the process

mk6-lp1.title: Nghe và chọn chi tiết
mk6-lp1.instr: Nghe từng đoạn và chọn đáp án đúng. Mỗi đoạn được nghe tối đa 2 lần.
mk6-lp1.body:
Listen to a message. Why can't the woman meet tomorrow?
W: Hi Dan, it's Lisa. I'm really sorry, but I can't meet for coffee tomorrow. I'm not ill or anything – my boss has asked me to go to a conference in Da Nang. Can we meet next week instead?
*She has to go on a work trip
She is ill
She has to work late
? "my boss has asked me to go to a conference".

A man is talking about his flat. How many bedrooms does it have?
M: The flat has a big living room, a kitchen and two bathrooms. There are three bedrooms, but we use the smallest one as an office.
*Three
Two
Four
? "There are three bedrooms".

Listen to two people in a shop. How much does the woman pay?
W: How much is this lamp?
M: It's thirty pounds, but everything's twenty percent off today.
W: Great, so that's twenty-four pounds. I'll take it.
*£24
£30
£20
? 30 – 20% = 24.

Listen to an announcement at an airport. What should passengers for flight BA 207 do?

*Go to gate 14
Go to gate 9
Wait for more information
? "go to gate 14 immediately".

Listen to a woman talking about her weekend. What did she enjoy most?
W: On Saturday, we went to a new restaurant, which was OK. But the highlight was Sunday afternoon, when we went to see a play at the theatre. The actors were brilliant.

Eating at a restaurant
Going shopping

The membership price
The location

M: Sorry, I won't have the car. What about a dessert? I can carry a cake easily.
W: Perfect.

Drinks
Meat

Listen to a teacher. When is the school trip?

Wednesday the 10th
Friday the 10th
? Dời sang thứ Sáu ngày 12.

Listen to a woman describing a lost bag. What colour is it?
W: I left my bag on the train. It's a black backpack with a red stripe on the front, and there's a green water bottle in the side pocket.
*Black
Red
Green
? "It's a black backpack".

Listen to a radio interview. What does the man do now?
M: I trained as an engineer and worked in that field for ten years. Then I retrained, and now I'm a primary school teacher. My wife, by the way, is still an engineer.
*He is a teacher
He is an engineer
He is a student
? "now I'm a primary school teacher".

Listen to a message from a bank. What does the customer need to do?
W: This is a message from City Bank. Your new card is ready. Please visit your local branch with your passport to collect it. You don't need to make an appointment.
*Go to the bank with a passport
Make an appointment
Call the bank
? "visit your local branch with your passport".

Listen to a woman talking about a course. Why did she choose it?
W: There were cheaper courses, and some closer to home. But this one had small classes – only eight students – so I knew I'd get lots of attention from the teacher.
*It has small classes
It is cheap
It is near her home
? "this one had small classes".

Listen to two colleagues. What is the woman worried about?
M: Are you ready for the presentation?
W: The slides are finished and I've practised a lot. I just hope the projector works this time – it broke down last week in the middle of a meeting.
*The equipment
Her slides
Her preparation
? Lo máy chiếu hỏng.

mk6-lp2.title: Ghép người nói
mk6-lp2.instr: Four people are talking about moving to a new city. Match each speaker with what they say. There are two extra options.
mk6-lp2.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Finding a home was difficult | I miss my family | I moved for my partner | It is cheaper than before | The weather is a problem | The people are very friendly
Speaker A = Finding a home was difficult
W: When I first arrived, I spent two months living in a hostel. Every flat I looked at was either too expensive or already taken by the time I called. In the end, a colleague told me about a room in her building, and I was so relieved.
Speaker B = The weather is a problem
M: I love my job here, and the city is beautiful. But I grew up somewhere hot and sunny, and here it rains almost every day in winter. I've bought three umbrellas already, and I still find the grey skies depressing.
Speaker C = I moved for my partner
W: I was perfectly happy in my hometown, to be honest. But my husband got an amazing job offer here, and we decided it was too good to refuse. I'm still looking for work myself, but I'm sure I'll find something soon.
Speaker D = The people are very friendly
M: I was worried that a big city would feel cold and unwelcoming. But my neighbours invited me for dinner in my first week, and people in the shops always stop for a chat. I've never felt lonely here.

mk6-lp3.audio:
M: My nephew's only eight and he's already got his own smartphone. I think that's far too young.
W: I don't know. Parents want to be able to contact their kids, especially when they travel to school alone.
M: They could give them a basic phone for calls, though. They don't need the internet.
W: That's fair. The real danger is all the social media apps.
M: Exactly. And kids spend so much time on screens that they don't play outside any more.
W: I'm not sure that's the phone's fault. Parents need to set limits.
M: Well, I agree that parents have to take responsibility.

mk6-lp3.body:

Eight-year-olds are too young for smartphones. = Man
Phones help parents stay in contact with children. = Woman
Social media is the biggest risk for children. = Both
Parents must control how children use phones. = Both

mk6-lp4a.audio: M: For decades, parks were the first thing to be cut when city budgets were tight. They were seen as nice to have, but not essential. I think the pandemic changed that view completely. When people were stuck at home, parks became the only place they could exercise, meet friends safely or simply escape their small flats. Now research is confirming what many of us suspected: people who live near green spaces are healthier and less stressed. My concern is that new parks are mostly built in wealthy areas, while poorer neighbourhoods, where people often have no garden or balcony, still have the least green space.
mk6-lp4a.title: Bài nói 1
mk6-lp4a.instr: Listen to a city planner talking about public parks. Answer two questions.
mk6-lp4a.body:
According to the planner, how have attitudes to parks changed?
*They are now seen as essential
They are seen as too expensive
People use them less than before
? "parks were… nice to have, but not essential. I think the pandemic changed that view".

What is the planner concerned about?
*Parks are unequally distributed
Parks are badly maintained
Parks are too crowded
? "new parks are mostly built in wealthy areas".

mk6-lp4b.audio: W: My first business was an online clothing shop, and it failed after eighteen months. At the time, I felt ashamed, and I hid it from friends. Looking back, it was the most valuable experience of my career. I learned how to manage money, how to deal with suppliers and, most importantly, that I had tried to do everything myself. In my current company, I hired people with skills I don't have from the very start. I do think, though, that our education system teaches young people to avoid failure at all costs. Until schools reward taking risks, many talented people will never try to start a business.
mk6-lp4b.title: Bài nói 2
mk6-lp4b.instr: Listen to a young business owner talking about failure. Answer two questions.
mk6-lp4b.body:
How does the speaker now feel about her first business?
*It taught her important lessons
She is still ashamed of it
It was a waste of time
? "it was the most valuable experience of my career".

What does she criticise?
*Schools discourage risk-taking
Banks refuse to lend money
Young people are lazy
? "our education system teaches young people to avoid failure at all costs".

mk6-w3.body:
NGƯỜI HỎI: Rosa
CÂU HỎI: Hi! Have you ever visited an art gallery? Tell us about it.
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi Rosa! Yes, I visited the Fine Arts Museum in Hanoi last year. I enjoyed it because the lacquer paintings were beautiful. I also learned a lot about Vietnamese history from the old paintings there.

NGƯỜI HỎI: Leo
CÂU HỎI: I want to start painting but I'm not creative. What should I do?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi Leo! I suggest copying simple pictures from books at first. I recommend this because it helps you learn basic skills. For example, you could paint fruit or flowers before trying your own ideas.

NGƯỜI HỎI: Kim
CÂU HỎI: Should art be a compulsory subject at school? What do you think?
SỐ TỪ: 30-40
BÀI MẪU: Hi Kim! Yes, I think art should be compulsory at primary school. I believe this because it develops children's creativity. However, older students should be able to choose, because they need time for exam subjects.

mk6-w4.intro: Email từ câu lạc bộ: "Dear member, The Art Club is planning an exhibition of members' work at the end of the year. We have not yet decided where to hold it or whether to sell the paintings. We would like to know your opinion."
mk6-w4.title: Viết 2 email
mk6-w4.instr: Email cho bạn khoảng 50 từ (thân mật) và email cho quản lý 120–150 từ (trang trọng). Khoảng 30 phút.
mk6-w4.body:
CÂU HỎI: Write an email to your friend, who is also a member of the club. Write about your feelings and what you will show at the exhibition.
SỐ TỪ: 40-50
BÀI MẪU: Hi Mai,
I'm really excited about the club's exhibition at the end of the year.
I think it's a great chance to show our work to the public.
I'm considering showing my paintings of the old town.
What do you think?
Love,
Thao

CÂU HỎI: Write an email to the club manager. Write about your feelings and your suggestions for the location and selling the paintings.
SỐ TỪ: 120-150
BÀI MẪU: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to share my thoughts about the members' exhibition planned for the end of the year. I am very pleased that the club is giving us the opportunity to show our work.
I would like to suggest holding the exhibition in the city library, which has a large hall and many visitors every day. I believe we should also sell the paintings and give part of the money to a local charity. However, some members may not want to sell their work.
If the library is unavailable, we could ask a local café to display the paintings for a month. I also suggest letting each artist decide whether their work is for sale, so that everyone feels comfortable taking part.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Pham Thao

mk6-s1.title: Câu hỏi cá nhân
mk6-s1.instr: Trả lời từng câu hỏi trong khoảng 30 giây.
mk6-s1.body:
CÂU HỎI: Please tell me about your job or studies. | 30
BÀI MẪU: I'm currently working as an accountant for a logistics company. My main tasks are checking invoices and preparing monthly reports. The work can be repetitive, but I like it because I'm good with numbers and my colleagues are supportive. In the future, I'd like to get an international qualification.
CÂU HỎI: What did you do last weekend? | 30
BÀI MẪU: Last weekend was quite relaxing. On Saturday morning, I went to a yoga class, and in the afternoon I helped my mother cook a big family meal. On Sunday, I met some old friends at a café, and we spent hours talking about our plans for the new year.
CÂU HỎI: What kind of films do you like? | 30
BÀI MẪU: I really enjoy animated films and comedies, because they make me laugh and forget about my worries. I also like documentaries about nature. I usually watch films at home with English subtitles, which is a fun way to improve my listening skills.

mk6-s2.part: Part 2 · Describe, express opinion, give reasons
mk6-s2.title: Mô tả ảnh
mk6-s2.instr: Mô tả bức ảnh rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Nội dung ảnh được mô tả bằng chữ.
mk6-s2.body:
ẢNH: Một người bán hàng rong đang nấu ăn tại một quầy nhỏ trên vỉa hè buổi tối; vài khách ngồi trên ghế nhựa thấp chờ đồ ăn.
CÂU HỎI: Describe this picture. | 45
BÀI MẪU: This picture shows a street food stall in the evening. A middle-aged woman is cooking something in a large pan – it looks like noodles or fried rice – and there's steam coming from it. In front of her, several customers are sitting on small plastic stools, waiting for their food. Some of them are chatting, and one man is looking at his phone. The street is lit by lamps and the lights from shops, so the atmosphere looks warm and lively. I think this is probably in Vietnam or another Asian country.
CÂU HỎI: Why is street food popular in many countries? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I think street food is popular for three main reasons. First, it's cheap, so students and workers can eat well without spending much. Second, it's fast, which is perfect for busy people. Third, it's often delicious and authentic, because many sellers have cooked the same dish for years. Tourists also love street food, because it allows them to experience local culture in a very direct way.
CÂU HỎI: Is street food safe to eat? What do you think? | 45
BÀI MẪU: In most cases, I think it's safe, but you need to be careful. I always choose stalls that are busy, because that means the food is fresh and local people trust it. I avoid places where the food has been sitting out for a long time. In my opinion, the government should also check hygiene regularly and train sellers, so that customers can feel more confident.

mk6-s3.title: So sánh hai ảnh
mk6-s3.instr: Mô tả và so sánh hai bức ảnh, rồi trả lời các câu hỏi, mỗi câu khoảng 45 giây. Nội dung ảnh được mô tả bằng chữ.
mk6-s3.body:
ẢNH: Ảnh 1: Hành khách ngồi trên máy bay, nhìn qua cửa sổ thấy mây.
ẢNH: Ảnh 2: Một đoàn tàu chạy qua cánh đồng xanh, hành khách ngồi đọc sách và ngắm cảnh.
CÂU HỎI: Tell me what you see in the two pictures. | 45
BÀI MẪU: Both pictures show people travelling, but in different ways. The first picture was taken inside an airplane. The passengers are sitting in narrow seats, and through the window I can see white clouds, so the plane is flying high. The second picture shows a train travelling through green countryside. Inside, passengers look relaxed – one is reading a book and another is looking out at the view. Overall, the plane looks faster but more cramped, while the train looks slower but more comfortable.
CÂU HỎI: Which way of travelling do you prefer? Why? | 45
BÀI MẪU: For long distances, I usually prefer flying, because it saves a lot of time. For example, flying from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City takes about two hours, while the train takes more than thirty. However, for shorter trips, I love taking the train. It's more relaxing, I can move around, and I can enjoy the scenery along the way, which makes the journey part of the holiday.
CÂU HỎI: How will people travel in the future? | 45
BÀI MẪU: I think travel will become faster and greener. Many countries are building high-speed railways, which could replace short flights. Electric cars and buses will probably become normal in cities. Some people even talk about electric planes for short distances. On the other hand, because of climate change, governments may make flying more expensive, so people might travel less often but stay longer in each place.

mk6-s4.title: A disappointing experience
mk6-s4.instr: Chuẩn bị 1 phút (được ghi chú), sau đó nói 2 phút trả lời cả 3 câu.
mk6-s4.body:
ẢNH: Một người đang đứng dưới mưa trước một sân khấu ngoài trời vắng tanh, tay cầm vé.
CHUẨN BỊ: 60
NÓI: 120
CÂU HỎI: Tell me about a time when you were disappointed.
BÀI MẪU: I'd like to talk about a time when a concert I'd been waiting for was cancelled. Two years ago, my favourite band announced a show in Ho Chi Minh City. I bought tickets months in advance and booked a flight with my best friend. But on the day of the concert, a huge storm hit the city, and the organisers cancelled the event just one hour before it started.
CÂU HỎI: How did you deal with that feeling?
BÀI MẪU: At first, I was really upset, because I had spent a lot of money and been looking forward to it for so long. But my friend and I decided to make the most of the trip. We explored the city, tried lots of street food and visited museums. In the end, it became one of my favourite trips, even without the concert.
CÂU HỎI: Is it good for young people to experience disappointment? Why?
BÀI MẪU: Yes, I believe it is, as long as it's not too serious. Disappointment teaches young people that life doesn't always go as planned, and it helps them become more resilient. If parents protect their children from every difficulty, those children may struggle to cope with problems when they grow up. Of course, adults should support them and help them learn from the experience, rather than leaving them to deal with it alone.

mk7-r2a.title: Sắp xếp câu: thuyết trình hiệu quả
mk7-r2a.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại thành đoạn văn hợp lý.
mk7-r2a.body:
Giving a presentation can be stressful, but good preparation makes it much easier.
Start by deciding on the one main message you want your audience to remember.
Then organise your ideas into three or four clear sections that support this message.
Keep your slides simple, with a few key words and images rather than long sentences.
Finally, rehearse the whole talk aloud several times, ideally in front of a friend.
Their feedback will show you which parts are unclear before the real event.

mk7-r2b.title: Sắp xếp câu: tìm lại người bạn cũ
mk7-r2b.instr: Câu đầu tiên đã cho sẵn. Sắp xếp 5 câu còn lại thành đoạn văn hợp lý.
mk7-r2b.body:
When I was ten, my best friend Hana moved to another country with her family.
We wrote letters for a year or two, but then we lost contact.
Last spring, I decided to search for her name on social media.
After hours of looking, I found a profile with a photo that looked just like her.
Nervously, I sent her a message, and she replied the same evening.
This summer, we finally met again after twenty years, and it felt as if no time had passed.

mk7-r3.intro:
Sarah: Our company tried a four-day week last year, and I was surprised how well it worked. We cut unnecessary meetings and focused on what really mattered. I now spend Fridays with my elderly father, which wasn't possible before.

Hieu: I own a small restaurant, and for me it simply isn't realistic. Customers expect us to be open seven days a week. If my staff worked one day less, I would have to hire more people, and I can't afford that.

Anna: I like the idea in theory, but in practice my workload stayed the same. I was trying to do five days of work in four, so I came home exhausted every evening. After a few months, I asked to return to my old schedule.

Michael: As an economist, I think the evidence is promising but limited. Most trials have been in office jobs, where it's easy to measure results. We need more research in sectors like healthcare and manufacturing before governments make any decisions.

mk7-r4.title: Ghép tiêu đề: khoa học về hạnh phúc
mk7-r4.instr: Bài đọc dài khoảng 750 từ như đề thật. Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Có 8 tiêu đề cho 7 đoạn, một tiêu đề thừa.
mk7-r4.body:
LỰA CHỌN: Doing good feels good | Experiences over possessions | Money matters, up to a point | Relationships are the key | The happiest countries | The problem with comparing | A new area of science | Happiness can be learned
For centuries, happiness was a subject for philosophers and religious leaders rather than scientists. That began to change in the late twentieth century, when psychologists decided to study what makes people flourish, not only what makes them ill. Since then, thousands of studies have been carried out, using surveys, brain scans and long-term studies that follow the same people for decades. Governments have also become interested, and several now measure the wellbeing of their citizens alongside economic growth. The results are often surprising, and they challenge many of our common beliefs about what makes a good life. Some countries have even appointed ministers whose job is to improve the happiness and wellbeing of the population. = A new area of science
The most obvious question is whether money makes us happier. The answer appears to be yes, but only to a certain extent. For people who struggle to pay for food, housing and healthcare, extra income makes a huge difference to their wellbeing. Once basic needs are comfortably met, however, the effect becomes much smaller. A large pay rise may bring a short burst of pleasure, but most people quickly get used to their new standard of living, and their happiness returns to roughly the same level as before. This process, which psychologists call adaptation, helps to explain why lottery winners are often no happier a few years after their win. = Money matters, up to a point
How we spend money also seems to matter. Research suggests that people get more lasting satisfaction from buying experiences, such as holidays, concerts or courses, than from buying objects. A new phone or car is exciting at first, but the excitement fades as it becomes part of everyday life. Experiences, on the other hand, become part of our personal story. We remember them, talk about them with others and often value them more as time passes, even if they did not go perfectly at the time. Shared experiences seem to be especially valuable, because they also strengthen our relationships with the people we enjoy them with. = Experiences over possessions
One reason that money does not always bring happiness is our tendency to compare ourselves with others. People tend to judge their income, appearance and achievements against those of friends, neighbours and colleagues. Social media has made this much worse, since we now see a constant stream of other people's holidays, parties and successes, carefully selected to look perfect. Several studies have linked heavy use of social media with lower life satisfaction, particularly among young people, who are more sensitive to how they compare with their peers. Some psychologists recommend limiting time on these platforms, or at least remembering that what we see online is rarely the whole picture. = The problem with comparing
If one finding stands out above all others, it is the importance of close relationships. One of the longest studies of adult life, which has followed hundreds of people for more than eighty years, concluded that the quality of people's relationships was the strongest predictor of their happiness and even their physical health in old age. It was not the number of friends that mattered, but whether people had someone they could rely on. Loneliness, in contrast, has been shown to be as harmful to health as smoking. For this reason, some doctors now ask patients about their social lives as well as their diet and exercise habits. = Relationships are the key
Helping others is another reliable source of happiness. In one well-known experiment, participants were given a small amount of money and told either to spend it on themselves or on someone else. Those who spent it on others reported feeling happier at the end of the day. Volunteering has similar effects, and people who regularly volunteer tend to report better health and a stronger sense of purpose. Scientists believe that acts of kindness strengthen our social connections, which links back to the importance of relationships. Interestingly, the amount of money or time given seems to matter less than the act of giving itself. = Doing good feels good
Perhaps the most encouraging message from this research is that happiness is not completely fixed. Our genes and circumstances certainly play a part, but a significant portion seems to depend on our habits and the way we think. Simple activities such as writing down three things we are grateful for each day, exercising regularly and spending time in nature have been shown to improve wellbeing over time. Happiness, it seems, is not just something that happens to us, but also a skill that we can practise. None of these habits is a magic solution, but together they suggest that small, regular changes can gradually make a real difference. = Happiness can be learned
